brief_summary: This study aims to examine and compare static and dynamic inspiratory muscle strength and cardiorespiratory fitness in adults with cystic fibrosis and their healthy peers.
title: Assessment of Static and Dynamic Inspiratory Muscle Strength and Cardiorespiratory Fitness in Adults With Cystic Fibrosis

brief_summary: The hypothesis of this study is that intraoperative intravenous lidocaine infusion provides postoperative analgesia and opioid-sparing effects that are at least equivalent to those achieved with a bilateral erector spinae plane block, while offering a simpler and faster procedure that does not require ultrasound guidance and whose efficacy is not dependent on operator expertise or on the uncertain spread of local anesthetic injection in the lumbar region.
lead_sponsor: GCS Ramsay Santé pour l'Enseignement et la Recherche
primary_outcomes: Total morphine consumption within 48 hours after surgery, expressed in milligrams (mg), calculated as the cumulative consumption of intravenous (IV) morphine administered in the PACU and oral morphine converted to IV morphine equivalents.
title: Intravenous Lidocaine Versus Erector Spinae Plane Block After Lumbar Arthrodesis (LIBERA)

brief_summary: This study is a randomized controlled experimental clinical trial designed to investigate the effects of visual and auditory stimulation on dyspnea severity, sleep quality, and anxiety levels in patients receiving noninvasive mechanical ventilation (NIMV) support in a secondary-level cardiac intensive care unit. A total of 44 patients (22 in the intervention group, 22 in the control group) are planned to be included in the study. Patients in the intervention group will be exposed to images of the Northern Lights projected onto the ceiling and white noise simultaneously for 30 minutes each night over two nights. The control group will receive no intervention other than routine nursing care. Data will be collected using the Dyspnea-12 Scale, the State Anxiety Inventory, the Richards-Campbell Sleep Scale, and a physiological parameters form. The study results are expected to contribute to evidence-based practices aimed at reducing dyspnea and anxiety, improving sleep quality, and enhancing patient comfort in intensive care patients through non-pharmacological methods.
interventions: The Northern Lights and White Noise
primary_outcomes: Effect of Northern Lights and White Noise on Dyspnea: Dyspnea-12 (D-12)
Effect of Northern Lights and White Noise on Anxiety: State Anxiety Inventory
Effect of Northern Lights and White Noise on Sleep Quality: Richards-Campbell Sleep Questionnaire (RCSQ)
Effect of Northern Lights and White Noise on Pulse Rate
Effect of Northern Lights and White Noise on Blood Pressure
title: Visual and Auditory Stimulation in Intensive Care Patients

brief_summary: This is a randomized, multicenter, phase III clinical study to compare the efficacy and safety of perioperative treatment with adebrelimab plus platinum-based chemotherapy versus adebrelimab adjuvant therapy in patients with resectable stage II-IIIB non-small-cell lung cancer(NSCLC).
title: A Study of Perioperative Adebrelimab Plus Chemotherapy Versus Adjuvant Therapy in Patients With Resectable NSCLC

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to examine whether individuals with co-occurring opioid use disorder and alcohol use (OUD+ALC) experience heightened pain sensitivity, pain-related negative affect, and greater alcohol reinforcement compared with alcohol-only (ALC) or opioid-only (OUD-ALC) users.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Aim 1. Do individuals with OUD+ALC experience increased pain and pain-related negative affect during periods of sobriety relative to mono-users of alcohol (ALC only) and opioids (OUD-ALC)?
* Aim 2. Do individuals with OUD+ALC experience greater alcohol-induced analgesia and alcohol reinforcement compared with mono-users of alcohol (ALC only) and opioids (OUD-ALC)?

Participants will:

* Complete a screening session
* Complete one lab session including a comprehensive assessment battery involving multimodal assessments of pain during sobriety
* Complete two experimental lab sessions that will include intravenous (IV) administration of either 80mg% alcohol or placebo (saline), order counterbalanced, to measure alcohol's acute effects on pain and pain-related negative affect
primary_outcomes: Pain intensity during the pressure task, measured using a visual analog scale (VAS)
Pain pressure threshold during the pressure task
Startle eyeblink potentiation during the anticipation task
Self-reported affect during the anticipation task
Subjective affective response to alcohol in the lab
title: Pain Sensitivity, Alcohol-Induced Analgesia, and Heavy Drinking in Individuals With Opioid Use Disorder

brief_summary: The researchers are doing this study to find out whether the combination of ivermectin and standard of care prophylaxis (SOCP; drugs given to prevent the development of a disease or condition) is an effective treatment approach for people with skin side effects caused by daraxonrasib treatment (daraxonrasib-induced skin toxicity). The researchers will compare the combination of ivermectin and SOCP with SOCP alone to see which treatment approach is more effective. The researchers will also look at how the study treatments impact participants' quality of life. The researchers will measure quality of life by having participants complete questionnaires.
title: A Study of Standard of Care Drugs With or Without Ivermectin for Daraxonrasib-Induced Skin Toxicity in People With Pancreatic Cancer

brief_summary: This randomized, controlled non-inferiority trial will compare two established botulinum toxin injection techniques for adductor spasmodic dysphonia: percutaneous electromyography-guided injection and transnasal endoscopic catheter-guided injection. The study will evaluate whether the endoscopic technique provides voice outcomes that are not inferior to the standard EMG-guided approach, while also assessing treatment-related adverse effects, procedural tolerability, and practical advantages such as direct visualization and suitability for patients with challenging neck anatomy.
interventions: Intervention B - Endoscopic Catheter BTX Injection
primary_outcomes: Change from Baseline in Voice Handicap Index (VHI-30) at 4 weeks post-operation
title: EMG-Guided Versus Endoscopic-Catheter Botulinum Toxin Injection for Spasmodic Dysphonia

brief_summary:
CD180 is a cell-surface protein recently identified through proteomic analysis as a potential target of interest in myeloid hematological malignancies. It may have diagnostic and monitoring potential, particularly in acute myeloid leukemia (AML).

This monocentric, non-interventional, retrospective observational study aims to characterize CD180 expression by flow cytometry in pathological hematopoietic cells, particularly in AML, and in normal hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (CD34+ cells). The study will use residual blood and bone marrow samples collected during routine care and otherwise intended for disposal by incineration, together with relevant clinical and laboratory data.
conditions: Normal Hematopoietic Stem and Progenitor Cells
primary_outcomes: CD180 Expression in Normal and Pathological CD34+ Cells
title: Characterization of CD180 Protein Expression in Myeloid Hematological Malignancies by Flow Cytometry

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate whether Expand Your Horizon (EYH), a brief writing intervention focused on body functionality, can improve body image in university students aged 18 to 30 years in Spain and Argentina.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

Does EYH improve body appreciation and appreciation of body functionality compared with an active control condition?

Are changes in body image flexibility, self-compassion, and mentalization potential mechanisms underlying improvements in body image?

Researchers will compare EYH with an active control program involving creative writing exercises to evaluate the effects of the intervention.

Participants will:

Complete online questionnaires before the intervention, immediately after it, and one month later.

Complete three writing exercises over approximately five days. Participants in the EYH group will write about their body's functions and their personal meaning, while those in the control group will complete creative writing exercises.

Answer questions about their experience of the intervention, including satisfaction and acceptability.

Have their written responses to the EYH exercises analyzed qualitatively to explore how they describe and understand their bodies and body functionality.
title: Expand Your Horizon-Spanish

brief_summary:
The objective of this clinical trial is to determine whether virtual reality (VR) devices can improve comfort and quality of life in hospitalized adult patients with hematological malignancies who require at least 15 consecutive days of inpatient treatment. The study will include adult patients of both sexes with 18 years or more.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does the use of virtual reality devices improve the overall comfort of patients hospitalized with hematological malignancies?
* Does virtual reality improve patients' quality of life compared to standard clinical care without the use of this technology?
* What are the immediate effects of virtual reality on patient well-being, and what potential adverse effects may arise during its use?
* How do patients perceive the use of virtual reality during their hospital stay?

The researchers will compare two groups:

* Group A: Virtual reality intervention: Participants will use virtual reality devices for 15 minutes on days 5, 8, 15, and 22 of the study. They will be able to choose from a selection of virtual natural landscapes, providing an immersive distraction during their hospitalization.
* Group B: Control group: Participants will receive standard clinical care without the virtual reality intervention.

Participants will be randomly assigned to one of the two groups. Comfort and quality of life will be assessed using the General Comfort Questionnaire (GCQ) and the European Organisation for Research and Treatment of Cancer Quality of Life Questionnaire (EORTC QLQ-C30), both of which will be administered on days 5 and 22 of the study. Additionally, the immediate effects of virtual reality will be evaluated by measuring vital signs and assessing symptoms before and after the intervention, including any potential discomfort, dizziness, or nausea related to the use of this technology. The study aims to recruit approximately 145 participants across three hospitals in Valencia, Spain. The results could help determine whether virtual reality serves as a useful non-pharmacological nursing intervention for improving comfort and well-being during a prolonged hospital stay due to hematological malignancies.
lead_sponsor: Fundación para la Investigación del Hospital Clínico de Valencia
primary_outcomes: To determine the effectiveness of using VR headsets in improving the comfort of hematology patients during their hospital stay with the General Comfort Questionnaire (GCQ).
title: Virtual Reality Intervention to Improve Comfort in Hospitalized Hematology Patients.

brief_summary: More efficacious treatments for Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) in Veterans are urgently needed. Psilocybin is a promising novel treatment that is likely to be the first FDA-approved psychedelic, but its safety and efficacy remain unclear. To address this gap, the investigators propose a randomized controlled trial of a single dose of psilocybin paired with a brief course of a VA-endorsed evidence-based psychotherapy (Acceptance and Commitment Therapy) in Veterans with MDD. Our trial addresses key limitations of previous studies including the challenge of management of expectancy effects, a focus on Veterans with input from Veterans, and a study population that reflects the demographics and medical and psychiatric complexity of the VHA patient population. Our study also explores psilocybin's antidepressant mechanisms focusing on changes in psychological flexibility and synaptic plasticity. In sum, this study will provide critical and timely data to determine if psilocybin treatment is a safe and efficacious treatment for MDD in Veterans.
lead_sponsor: VA Office of Research and Development
title: Psilocybin for Depression in Veterans

brief_summary: This trial is a Phase III, randomized, open-label, multicenter study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of QLC5508 versus investigator's choice chemotherapy in participants with advanced EP-NEC that has failed after at least one prior platinum-based chemotherapy regimen.
interventions: Investigator's Choice Chemotherapy (FOLFIRI or FOLFOX regimen)
title: QLC5508 vs. Investigator's Choice Chemotherapy in Advanced Extrapulmonary Neuroendocrine Carcinoma

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether oral bromelain, a pineapple-derived enzyme supplement, reduces facial swelling, limited mouth opening (trismus), and pain after surgical removal of impacted lower wisdom teeth in healthy young adults. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does adding bromelain to standard postoperative medication reduce facial swelling and trismus?
* Does it reduce postoperative pain and the number of painkillers taken?

Researchers compared each patient's recovery after two separate operations: one followed by standard medication alone and one followed by standard medication plus bromelain.

Participants:

* Had both impacted lower wisdom teeth removed in two separate sessions about two weeks apart
* Took bromelain (500 mg twice daily for 5 days) after one randomly selected session
* Had facial swelling and mouth opening measured before surgery and on days 2 and 7
* Rated their pain at set times during the first week and recorded the painkillers they took
title: Oral Bromelain After Bilateral Mandibular Third Molar Surgery

interventions: Olorofim is a novel antifungal drug

brief_summary: This multicenter prospective observational cohort study aims to develop and validate individualized risk prediction models for stroke and cognitive decline in patients with moyamoya disease or moyamoya syndrome by integrating clinical characteristics, laboratory data, multimodal neuroimaging, genetic information, and other available multidimensional data. Approximately 3,000 participants will be enrolled and followed for up to 24 months.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of stroke within 24 months after enrollment
title: Development and Validation of Risk Prediction Models for Stroke and Cognitive Impairment in Moyamoya Disease and Moyamoya Syndrome

brief_summary: Poor sleep is common among people living with HIV and is linked to fatigue, psychological distress and poorer adherence to antiretroviral therapy. This study develops a mobile sleep hygiene mentor that uses artificial intelligence to give personalised sleep recommendations, with a dashboard that lets nurses follow participants and respond to risks. The mentor is built with adults living with HIV and HIV nurses and then tested for usability and feasibility. In the main evaluation, about 70 adults living with HIV with poor sleep use the mentor daily for four weeks, with two online nurse sessions, and are followed up four weeks later. The study measures sleep quality, insomnia severity, depression, anxiety and stress, fatigue, adherence to antiretroviral therapy, technology acceptance, engagement and safety.
title: AI-Powered Sleep Hygiene Mentor for Adults Living With HIV

brief_summary: This randomized controlled trial aims to compare open and laparoscopic repair of perforated duodenal ulcer in terms of postoperative outcomes. A total of 134 patients will be randomly allocated into two groups: Group A will undergo laparoscopic repair and Group B will undergo open repair. The study will evaluate and compare postoperative outcomes between the two surgical approaches.
interventions: Laparoscopic Repair of Perforated Duodenal Ulcer
Open Repair of Perforated Duodenal Ulcer
title: Comparison of Open vs Laparoscopic Repair of Perforated Duodenal Ulcer

title: Clinical Performance and Usability of the Heart Rate and Impedance Respiration Monitor Cable

brief_summary:
Bipolar enucleation of the prostate is an effective operation for men with urinary obstruction caused by a benign enlarged prostate. Some men leak urine for a period after the operation. Early apical release is a surgical step that frees the tip (apex) of the prostate at the start of the operation to reduce stretch on the urinary sphincter. The conventional technique cuts all the way around the apex, including the front (anterior) tissue next to the sphincter.

This randomized trial compares a modified technique, Anterior Bridge-Preserving Semicircular Early Apical Release (ABP-S-EAR), with conventional early apical release. ABP-S-EAR leaves the front tissue bridge between the 11 and 1 o'clock positions intact. Men aged 45 to 80 years scheduled for bipolar enucleation at Benha University Hospital, Egypt, will be randomly assigned to one technique. The main question is whether ABP-S-EAR improves urinary continence 1 month after surgery. The trial also compares patient-reported leakage, operative time, bleeding, catheter time, hospital stay, urinary symptoms, urine flow, and complications over 12 months.
conditions: Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms (LUTS) in Men With Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia (BPH)
interventions: Anterior Bridge-Preserving Semicircular Early Apical Release (ABP-S-EAR)
primary_outcomes: Proportion of Participants With Objective Urinary Continence at 1 Month
title: Anterior Bridge-Preserving Versus Conventional Early Apical Release in Bipolar Enucleation of the Prostate

brief_summary: Academic, independent, non-commercial, multicenter study sponsored by the Department of Translational Medical Sciences (DISMET), University of Naples Federico II. The study evaluates whether daily oral supplementation with Limosilactobacillus reuteri DSM 17938 and BG-R46 reduces crying and fussing time more rapidly than an indistinguishable placebo in otherwise healthy infants with Rome IV infantile colic.
interventions: Probiotic: L. reuteri DSM 17938 + BG-R46, total 2 × 10⁸ CFU/day
Placebo: matching oil formulation without L. reuteri
primary_outcomes: Daily total crying and fussing time at day 7
title: The Effect of Probiotics in Infantile Colic

brief_summary: The Functional Arm Scale for Throwers (FAST) is a patient-reported outcome measure that assesses upper extremity function in overhead throwing athletes. This methodological study aims to cross-culturally adapt the FAST into Turkish (FAST-TR) and to evaluate its validity and reliability. The adaptation process follows Beaton's guidelines, including forward translation, synthesis, back translation, expert committee review, and pretesting in 30 athletes. Overhead athletes aged 18 years or older who have regularly participated in at least one overhead sport for at least 3 years complete a demographic and sports information form, the FAST-TR, the Turkish versions of the Kerlan-Jobe Orthopaedic Clinic (KJOC) Shoulder and Elbow Score, and the Quick-DASH. A subgroup of participants completes the FAST-TR again 5 to 7 days later to assess test-retest reliability. Floor and ceiling effects, internal consistency, test-retest reliability, measurement error, construct validity, and known-groups validity between asymptomatic and symptomatic athletes are analyzed.
primary_outcomes: Functional Arm Scale for Throwers - Turkish Version (FAST-TR) Score
title: Cross-Cultural Adaptation, Validity, and Reliability of the Functional Arm Scale for Throwers (FAST) in Throwing Athletes

brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to find out whether it is safe to skip (omit) radiation therapy to the breast after lumpectomy in people with low-risk HER2-positive breast cancer who are receiving HER2-targeted therapy.
title: A Study of Skipping Radiation Therapy in People With Breast Cancer

brief_summary:
The goal of this Phase II, multicenter, open-label, randomized controlled trial is to evaluate the efficacy and safety of short-course treatment regimens for children with non-severe, drug-susceptible pulmonary tuberculosis.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Do the 3-month bedaquiline, delamanid, contezolid, and pyrazinamide regimen (BDCZ) and the 4-month fixed-dose combination (FDC) regimen provide effective treatment, as measured by tuberculosis-free survival at 12 months after treatment initiation?
* What are the safety profiles of the two short-course regimens, as measured by the incidence of grade 3 or higher adverse events?
* How do the short-course regimens compare with the standard 6-month treatment regimen in terms of treatment success, treatment failure, recurrence, and tuberculosis-free survival during follow-up?

Researchers will compare the 3-month BDCZ regimen and the 4-month FDC regimen with the standard 6-month treatment regimen to evaluate their efficacy and safety in children with non-severe, drug-susceptible pulmonary tuberculosis.

Participants will be randomly assigned to one of three treatment groups and will receive the allocated regimen. They will undergo clinical assessments and safety monitoring during treatment, with follow-up to assess treatment outcomes, tuberculosis recurrence, and tuberculosis-free survival at 12, 18, and 24 months after treatment initiation.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of grade 3 or higher adverse events
title: BRIGHT-Child TB: Short-Course Treatment for Non-Severe Pulmonary Tuberculosis in Children

brief_summary:
This retrospective observational study examines the association between the type of anesthesia used during cesarean delivery and early neonatal outcomes. The study includes newborns delivered by cesarean section at Bursa City Hospital between January 2020 and September 2026.

The investigators compare general anesthesia with neuraxial anesthesia (spinal, epidural, or combined spinal-epidural) in elective and emergency cesarean deliveries.

The primary outcome is a five-minute Apgar score below 7. Secondary outcomes include a one-minute Apgar score below 7, NICU admission within 24 hours after birth, and level of care, respiratory support and length of stay during that admission.

The study uses existing hospital records. No additional procedures or interventions are performed. The findings may help clarify how anesthesia type and the urgency of cesarean delivery are associated with early neonatal outcomes.
title: Anesthesia and Neonatal Outcomes After Cesarean Delivery

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate the superiority of the through codesign redesigned game joyVision over the iVision game for children with a cognitive age between 3 and 12 with CVI.

The main question it aims to answer is:

\- Does the joyVision game have a better adherence than the iVision game

Participants will play with both Ivision and joyVision for one month, in a randomized AB/BA sequence.
title: joyVision: The Superiority of Co-design in the Development of a Serious Game for Children With Cerebral Visual Impairment

brief_summary:
The Irish Perioperative OutcomeS (IPOS) Study aims to better understand the factors that influence recovery and outcomes in older adults undergoing major surgery in Ireland. As people live longer and more individuals have multiple long-term health conditions, increasing numbers of older patients require surgical treatment. These patients may be at greater risk of complications after surgery, including infections, heart problems, delirium (confusion), admission to intensive care, and death.

This study will collect information from routine medical records of patients aged 60 years and older who undergo major planned or emergency surgery in participating hospitals across Ireland. No changes will be made to patients' treatment or care, and no additional tests or procedures will be performed as part of the study.

Researchers will examine patient characteristics, health conditions, frailty, surgical factors, postoperative complications, and the level of care patients receive after surgery. The study will also evaluate whether access to critical care services and other healthcare resources affects outcomes.

The information gathered will help identify factors associated with better and worse surgical outcomes and may highlight opportunities to improve perioperative care for older patients. Findings from the study are expected to support healthcare planning, resource allocation, and quality improvement initiatives aimed at improving the safety and outcomes of surgery for older adults in Ireland.
conditions: Outcomes Following Major Surgery in Older Adults
title: The Irish Perioperative OutcomeS (IPOS) Study

brief_summary:
Peri-implant mucositis is an inflammatory condition affecting the soft tissues surrounding dental implants. Conventional non-surgical treatment is primarily based on mechanical removal of bacterial biofilm, although complete and sustained resolution of inflammation may not always be achieved.

This randomized controlled clinical trial aims to evaluate whether the use of diode laser therapy as an adjunct to conventional non-surgical mechanical treatment provides additional clinical and biological benefits in patients with peri-implant mucositis.

Participants will be randomly assigned to receive either conventional mechanical debridement alone or mechanical debridement combined with adjunctive diode laser therapy. Clinical outcomes, including bleeding on probing, plaque index, and probing depth, will be evaluated during a 12-month follow-up period. Biological changes will also be assessed through peri-implant crevicular fluid volume and matrix metalloproteinase-8 (MMP-8) levels.
title: Adjunctive Diode Laser Therapy for Peri-Implant Mucositis

brief_summary: The purpose of this clinical study is to determine if the study medicine NNC9836-0001 is safe and tolerable in healthy participants with overweight or obesity or who have type 2 diabetes (T2D). Participants will either get the study medicine NNC9836-0001 or placebo. Which treatment participants get is decided by chance. NNC9836-0001 is a new medicine aimed to treat type 2 diabetes.
primary_outcomes: Single ascending dose (SAD): Number of Treatment emergent adverse events (TEAEs)
Multiple ascending dose (MAD): Number of TEAEs
title: A Research Study to Check the Safety of NNC9836-0001 When Given to Healthy Participants and Participants With Type 2 Diabetes

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if the Gixam tongue-imaging test gives the same result each time it is done, in adults aged 45 to 84 who are at average risk for colorectal cancer and are scheduled for a screening colonoscopy. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does Gixam give the same result when the test is repeated on the same day, with the same device and the same staff member (repeatability)?
* Does Gixam give the same result when the test is done on different days, with different devices and different staff members (reproducibility)?

Participants will:

* Answer questions about their health, medicines, diet, alcohol and tobacco use, and oral care habits
* Have the Gixam tongue test 6 times over 2 weeks: 4 times on Day 1, once on Day 7 and once on Day 14
* On Days 7 and 14, report when they last ate, drank or smoked, and whether they brushed, scraped their tongue or used mouthwash
* Then join the main Gixam study (CL-1009) for a FIT stool test and their planned colonoscopy
primary_outcomes: Gixam repeatability - precision within-system-within-operator of all Runs
Gixam reproducibility - precision between-system-between-operator of all Systems/Operators
title: Evaluation of Gixam's Repeatability and Reproducibility Predicting the Presence of Advanced and Non-Advanced Colorectal Neoplasia

brief_summary: The OCUTOP is a new hand-held camera that photographs the front of the eye to map the shape of the cornea and to assess the tear film. Before it can be used in eye care it must be compared with the instruments that clinics already use. In this study, adults attending one of two UK eye clinics for an ordinary appointment are invited to have both eyes measured once with the OCUTOP and with the clinic's usual instruments, in a random order, and to complete two short questionnaires. The visit adds about 30 minutes; nothing is put in the eye and no treatment is given. The study measures how closely the OCUTOP agrees with the reference instruments for corneal curvature, tear break-up time and tear meniscus height, how repeatable it is, how often it produces usable images, how acceptable participants and clinicians find it, and whether any adverse events occur.
interventions: OCUTOP hand-held corneal topographer with OCUGRAPH software
Reference instrument measurement (corneal topography and tear-film assessment)
primary_outcomes: Agreement between the OCUTOP and the reference instrument for central simulated mean keratometry (K-mean)
Agreement between the OCUTOP and the reference instrument for first non-invasive tear break-up time (NIBUT-first)
Agreement between the OCUTOP and the reference instrument for average non-invasive tear break-up time (NIBUT-average)
Agreement between the OCUTOP and the reference instrument for central lower tear meniscus height (TMH)
title: Performance Evaluation of the OCUTOP Hand-held Corneal Topographer

brief_summary:
Brief Summary

This study aims to examine the effects of a six-week mindfulness training program on mindfulness, moral identity, and prosocial tendencies among undergraduate nursing students. Nursing students were randomly assigned to either an intervention group or a control group. Students in the intervention group participated in six weekly mindfulness sessions, supplemented by guided audio materials and opportunities for daily practice. Students in the control group participated in an alternative educational workshop.

The study outcomes were assessed before the intervention, immediately after the intervention, and at a two-month follow-up. The study seeks to determine whether mindfulness training can improve nursing students' mindfulness, moral identity, and prosocial tendencies over time. The findings may help inform the development of educational approaches to support nursing students' personal and professional development.
primary_outcomes: Change in prosocial tendencies scores from baseline to post-intervention and two-month follow-up
Change in mindfulness scores from baseline to post-intervention and two-month follow-up
Change in moral identity scores from baseline to post-intervention and two-month follow-up
title: Mindfulness Training to Promote Prosocial Tendencies in Nursing Students

brief_summary: The COVID-19 lockdown fostered unhealthy eating habits and reduced physical activity levels, leading to weight gain, sedentary behavior, and increased anxiety and sleep disorders. Consequently, this study aims to evaluate the efficacy of an intervention using motivational interviewing to promote healthy diet and physical activity, improve body weight, reduce anxiety and depression, and enhance sleep quality and overall quality of life among families in Baja California and Sonora, Mexico, following the COVID-19 lockdown. This randomized controlled trial will include 60 individuals and their families in an intervention group receiving the motivational interviewing approach, and another 60 individuals and their families in a comparison group receiving traditional nutritional counseling; both groups will receive the same information but through different strategies. The intervention will be conducted using the motivational interviewing approach, delivered by professionals trained in this strategy. During each session, families will receive information regarding a nutritional plan and healthy physical activity. The project will involve physicians, nutritionists, and psychologists, as well as interns from medical and nutrition academic programs. Following the information sessions-which will take place in person within the comfort of each family's home-participants will be asked if they wish to set individual or family goals to be achieved over the subsequent 15-day periods during the first five months, or 30-day periods during the final five months. The information shared with participants will be based on practical guidelines for chronic disease prevention issued by the Ministry of Health. Topics will include the importance of consuming fruits, vegetables, and fiber-rich foods; strategies to reduce the intake of high-fat foods and sugary beverages; and the physical and emotional health benefits of physical activity. At the start of the study, anthropometric measurements will be taken, and assessments will be conducted regarding diet, physical activity levels, anxiety, depression, sleep quality, and quality of life; upon completion of the 10-month intervention, all assessment tools will be administered again to evaluate potential differences in the variables of interest. It is expected that, by the end of the intervention, participants will be able to modify their dietary and physical activity habits to achieve and maintain a healthy body weight, and that the strategies employed over the 10 months will enable them to develop a long-term healthy lifestyle, helping to prevent physical and mental illnesses among the children, adolescents, and adults in each family.
title: Motivational Interviewing Intervention for Families With Overweight and Obesity

brief_summary: Evaluate the clinical efficacy and safety of the radiofrequency skin therapy device (model specification: RFM-01) produced by ReFumei (Hunan) Technology Co., Ltd. for improving facial skin wrinkles
interventions: Radiofrequency skin therapy equipment developed and produced by ReFumei (Hunan) Technology Co., Ltd. improves facial wrinkles

brief_summary: This is a single-center, prospective, longitudinal observational cohort study in adults with unruptured intracranial aneurysms (UIAs) who are managed by conservative observation rather than immediate surgery or endovascular treatment. The study aims to build a time-series dataset combining blood pressure variability (BPV) and three-dimensional (3D) aneurysm morphological evolution, and to develop deep-learning models using long short-term memory (LSTM) and Transformer networks to predict aneurysm rupture risk. A secondary aim is to compare the new models with traditional scores such as PHASES and to explore how BPV relates to 3D aneurysm change.Participants aged 18-80 years with UIA confirmed by CTA, MRA, or DSA and judged suitable for conservative follow-up will be enrolled consecutively at the study site. Those with imaging contraindications, other major cerebrovascular diseases such as moyamoya or arteriovenous malformation, or severe organ dysfunction are excluded. No study-driven intervention is imposed; routine clinical care continues. Baseline data include demographics, hypertension history, laboratory tests, 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure, home blood pressure for 7 days, optional wearable monitoring, and CTA/MRA/DSA for 3D aneurysm parameters such as volume, surface area, compactness, and sphericity. BPV is summarized using standard deviation, coefficient of variation, and variability independent of the mean.Participants scheduled for in-hospital visits provide written informed consent and are followed at 6, 12, 24, 36, 48, 72, 96, and 120 months with repeated BPV measurement and imaging. Participants who already have at least two qualifying imaging and blood-pressure records before enrollment and will not return for in-person visits provide verbal consent and are followed by telephone every 6-12 months to confirm health status and rupture/growth events. All data are entered into a REDCap system with automated and manual quality checks. A historical institutional dataset (CAIASA) may be used only for algorithm pretraining and is not counted as the prospective enrollment target.The primary outcome is UIA rupture confirmed by CT or surgery. Secondary outcomes include aneurysm growth defined as diameter increase ≥1 mm, changes in 3D morphological parameters over time, BPV trends, and incremental predictive performance versus PHASES using AUC, IDI, and NRI with bootstrapping validation. A data safety monitoring committee oversees safety and data integrity. Findings are expected to support individualized follow-up and treatment decisions for people with unruptured aneurysms.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of unruptured intracranial aneurysm rupture confirmed by CT or intraoperative findings
title: Prospective Observational Cohort Study for Predicting Unruptured Intracranial Aneurysm Rupture Risk Using Blood Pressure Variability and 3D Structural Evolution

brief_summary: This study will test whether a standardized ginger extract improves menstrual pain and related symptoms compared with placebo in women with painful periods. Participants aged 18 to 40 will be randomly assigned to ginger extract or placebo, then complete one menstrual cycle without study product to establish baseline. They will then take 2 capsules daily for two menstrual cycles. Neither participants nor the study team will know who receives which product. The study is conducted entirely remotely. Researchers will measure menstrual pain intensity and duration, rescue medication use, menstrual and premenstrual symptoms, and the impact of symptoms on daily life.

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to compare how four different ways of starting sevoflurane anaesthesia (the "wash-in" phase) affect the heart and circulation during the first 10 minutes after endotracheal intubation in adults undergoing elective major urological surgery. The main question it aims to answer is whether the wash-in strategy affects cardiac index 10 minutes after intubation. Researchers also compared other haemodynamic variables, the time needed to reach the target anaesthetic concentration (0.8 MAC), sevoflurane consumption, the need for ephedrine to treat low blood pressure, and depth of anaesthesia.

After a standard intravenous induction, participants were randomly assigned to one of four sevoflurane wash-in strategies: automated end-tidal-controlled delivery, or manual delivery with 0.5 L/min fresh gas flow and 8% sevoflurane, 1 L/min with 4% sevoflurane, or 2 L/min with 4% sevoflurane. Haemodynamic variables were measured continuously through a radial arterial line using the pressure recording analytical method (PRAM).
title: Haemodynamic Effects of Four Sevoflurane Wash-In Strategies After Tracheal Intubation

brief_summary:
The purpose of this randomized, single-blind comparative-effectiveness pilot study is to compare the effectiveness of two types of injections on pain and function over 6 months in patients with chronic discogenic (originating from the intervertebral discs) low back pain (LBP). Eligible participants will have failed an adequate trial of previous conservative treatments, had no prior surgery, and had no prior injections within the preceding 12 months of study participation.

One of the treatments in this study is called platelet-rich plasma (PRP). It uses a sample of a participant's own blood, which is spun in a machine to concentrate the platelets. These platelets are then injected into the participant's back to help healing and reduce pain and swelling. The other treatment available in this study uses donor tissue from the center of a spinal disc, called the nucleus pulposus (NP). This gel-like material normally helps absorb shock in the spine. In this therapy, NP tissue from a donor is injected into the damaged disc to help restore its cushioning function and replace lost tissue. In this study, participants will be randomly assigned to receive one of the two injections (either PRP or NP) to treat chronic discogenic LBP. In order to limit bias in outcome data, participants will not know what injection they received until 6 months post-procedure.

Participants will be asked to complete between 5-6 in-person visits with the study team. Beyond procedure-related activities including a blood draw and injection, participants will also complete questionnaires and physical examinations at the respective study visits.
lead_sponsor: Walter Reed National Military Medical Center
primary_outcomes: Between-Group Difference in Mean Change in Average LBP (NPRS)
title: PRP Versus NP Injections for Chronic Discogenic Low Back Pain

Participants will be assigned to either a HIIT group or a non-training control group. The control group did not participate in the training intervention and maintained its usual daily activities.

brief_summary:
This study evaluates whether testing fresh tumor samples outside the body can help guide treatment selection for patients with hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer that has progressed during endocrine therapy.

A biopsy sample from each participant will be tested using an ex vivo organ culture (EVOC) platform, which preserves the tumor tissue and allows researchers to assess its response to different anticancer treatments. The results will be used to help select the participant's next systemic treatment.

The main objective is to evaluate the proportion of patients whose cancer responds to treatment selected using this approach. The study will also assess how long the cancer remains controlled, overall survival, and the relationship between laboratory test results and clinical outcomes.

brief_summary:
This study aims to investigate whether the administration of a neuromuscular blocking agent (rocuronium) improves the anatomical positioning of a third-generation video laryngeal mask airway (video LMA) in adult patients undergoing elective surgery under general anesthesia.

A laryngeal mask airway is a device placed in the throat to maintain an open airway and support ventilation during general anesthesia. The third-generation video LMA incorporates a camera that allows the anesthesiologist to visualize the laryngeal structures and assess device positioning during insertion. Neuromuscular blocking agents reduce muscle tone and may facilitate airway device insertion. However, their potential benefits for the positioning and performance of video LMAs remain unclear.

This is a prospective, randomized, controlled, parallel-group, outcome assessor-blinded clinical trial. Eligible patients will be randomly assigned to one of two groups. Both groups will receive propofol and remifentanil for anesthesia induction. The intervention group will additionally receive rocuronium (0.6 mg/kg), while the control group will receive no neuromuscular blocking agent.

The primary outcome is the proportion of patients achieving optimal anatomical positioning of the video LMA, defined as a Brimacombe score of 4 on the integrated video image. Secondary outcomes include oropharyngeal leak pressure, insertion time, first-attempt insertion success, number of insertion attempts, ease of insertion, hemodynamic changes, ventilation parameters, airway-related complications, and postoperative adverse effects.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of Patients With Optimal Video LMA Position (Brimacombe-Berry Score 4)
title: Effect of Neuromuscular Blocking Agent Use on Video Laryngeal Mask Airway Insertion

brief_summary:
Sepsis is a life-threatening condition caused by a dysregulated immune response to infection, leading to organ dysfunction and increased mortality. Early diagnosis and accurate assessment of disease progression remain challenging. EMR3 (ADGRE3), a receptor expressed on the surface of neutrophils, may serve as a potential biomarker for sepsis diagnosis, immune response monitoring, and prognosis assessment. However, its clinical value requires further validation in large, multicenter prospective studies.

This multicenter, prospective, observational study will enroll approximately 3,000 adults across 8-15 hospitals in China. Participants will be classified into four groups: patients with sepsis or septic shock, patients with infection without sepsis, patients with noninfectious critical illnesses, and healthy or elective surgical controls. Neutrophil EMR3 expression will be measured using flow cytometry on residual blood samples obtained during routine clinical care. Patients with sepsis will undergo repeated measurements at baseline, 72 ± 12 hours, and day 7 ± 1 day, with an optional assessment at day 14 ± 2 days. Other participants will undergo baseline testing only. All participants will receive standard clinical care without study-related interventions or additional blood collection.

The primary outcome is the diagnostic accuracy of baseline neutrophil EMR3 expression for identifying sepsis, assessed by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Secondary outcomes include changes in EMR3 expression over time, associations with 28-day all-cause mortality, septic shock, organ dysfunction, secondary infections, and intensive care unit length of stay. The study will also compare EMR3 with established biomarkers, including CD64, HLA-DR, procalcitonin, C-reactive protein, and lactate, and evaluate whether incorporating EMR3 into combined models improves diagnostic and prognostic performance. This study aims to determine whether neutrophil EMR3 can serve as a reliable biomarker for early sepsis diagnosis, disease monitoring, and risk stratification.
primary_outcomes: Diagnostic Accuracy of Neutrophil EMR3 Expression for Sepsis
title: Clinical Value of EMR3 in Sepsis Diagnosis, Monitoring, and Prognosis: A Multicenter Prospective Observational Study

brief_summary:

Researchers review existing dental records and images obtained for clinical care and collect information during long-term follow-up. Enrollment has closed, and follow-up data collection is ongoing. Participants undergo intraoral scanning, oral and periodontal examinations, and questionnaires after providing written informed consent.

The study assesses the volume and thickness of augmented hard tissues, bone levels around implants, and surrounding soft tissues. It also assesses implant and restoration survival, health around implants, complications, and patient-reported outcomes. Researchers will explore factors associated with long-term tissue stability.

brief_summary: This is a multicenter, open-label, single-arm, prospective phase II clinical study. Eligible patients with lymph node-positive biliary tract cancer will undergo primary tumor resection with selective lymph node dissection. During surgery, the regional and retroperitoneal lymph nodes will be explored, and lymph nodes that are technically amenable to surgical resection will be dissected. Metastatic lymph nodes that cannot be safely or completely resected because of local invasion or because of their location beyond the feasible surgical dissection field will not be surgically resected and will subsequently be treated with postoperative radiotherapy. Following surgery, patients will receive postoperative radiotherapy to the primary tumor bed and involved/regional lymph node areas. For patients who undergo R0 or R1 resection, concurrent chemoradiotherapy with capecitabine or S-1 will be administered for 2 cycles, followed by 6 cycles of adjuvant chemotherapy. For patients who undergo R2 resection, concurrent radiotherapy with capecitabine or S-1, with or without a PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor, will be administered, followed by maintenance therapy with capecitabine or S-1, with or without a PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor, until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity.

brief_summary: The seasonality of affective disorders-particularly depressive symptoms-is well-documented in adults, yet it remains under-researched in adolescents. Recent studies, however, suggest that young people aged 11 to 20 experience marked seasonal fluctuations in mood. In both hospital pediatric settings and the ECLIPSE program, many adolescents are admitted due to depressive symptoms or suicidal crises; however, the role of seasonality in these cases remains largely unexplored. ECLIPSE (a Child and Adolescent Psychiatry Liaison and Emergency Consultation Team) is a service at the Rouen University Hospital dedicated to providing emergency and post-emergency care for children and adolescents experiencing psychological distress. It is designed for minors aged 3 to 16 whose psychological state requires prompt intervention, but not hospitalization. Clinical observation suggests that, for some patients, depressive manifestations follow an annual cycle. Identifying such seasonal patterns could help improve our understanding of vulnerability factors and enable the adaptation of prevention and care strategies. The Seasonal Pattern Assessment Questionnaire (SPAQ) (Reynaud et al., 2022)-used in adults (\>18 years old) to screen for seasonal affective disorder via a Global Seasonality Score (GSS)-is a simple, self-administered tool that can easily be used with adolescents. Its application in this context would allow for the assessment of the seasonality of depressive symptoms within this hospitalized population.
interventions: Measuring the intensity of the seasonality of depressive symptoms in adolescents
primary_outcomes: To assess the intensity of the seasonality of depressive symptoms in adolescents receiving care for child psychiatric reasons at the Rouen University Hospital
title: Assessment of the Seasonality of Depressive Symptoms in Adolescents

brief_summary:
The primary aim of this study is to evaluate the effect of structured clinical teaching scenarios on male nursing students' competence-including knowledge, self-confidence, and practical performance-in maternity care.

In many countries, including Egypt, male nursing students face significant barriers during obstetric and gynecological clinical rotations due to cultural beliefs, patient preferences, and traditional gender perceptions. These limitations restrict opportunities for direct hands-on practice, which can negatively affect students' clinical confidence and procedural skills.

To address these educational gaps, this quasi-experimental study utilizes a one-group pre-test/post-test design. A total of 150 male undergraduate nursing students enrolled in the maternity nursing clinical course at Delta University for Science and Technology, Egypt, will participate in structured scenario-based clinical teaching and simulation training. Clinical competence, practical skills, self-confidence, and learning satisfaction will be assessed before and immediately after the educational intervention using an Objective Structured Clinical Examination (OSCE), standardized performance checklists, and validated satisfaction and confidence scales.
interventions: Structured Scenario-Based Clinical Teaching in Maternity Care
lead_sponsor: Delta University for Science and Technology
primary_outcomes: Change in Objective Structured Clinical Examination (OSCE) Total Score

brief_summary:
Difficult intubation remains a clinically significant challenge in anesthetic practice, particularly among patients with obesity and altered body composition. Traditional predictors such as BMI and neck circumference have limitations in accurately identifying at-risk patients.

The weight-adjusted waist circumference index (WWI), introduced by Park et al., provides a measure of age-related changes in body composition, including loss of muscle mass and retention or increase in fat mass. Some researchers have proposed a cut-off value of 10.4 cm/√kg in men and 10.5 cm/√kg in women to identify unhealthy body composition. WWI provides a clearer picture of fat distribution, especially in individuals with varying body sizes, making it a more reliable tool for assessing health risks related to abdominal fat. After a thorough literature review, studies correlating WWI with DI remain limited. Therefore, the present study aimed to assess the correlation between WWI and DI in 50 patients scheduled for elective surgeries requiring endotracheal intubation under direct laryngoscopy.

title: Association of WWI With Difficult Intubation

brief_summary:

* How does this program compare with a resistance training program designed by a professional coach and with no structured resistance training? Researchers will compare three groups: an artificial intelligence-generated resistance training group, a coach-designed resistance training group, and a non-exercising control group.

Participants in the two training groups will complete supervised resistance training three times per week for eight weeks. Participants in the control group will not take part in structured resistance training. brief_summary:
Background and study aims

Hearing problems are becoming more common. In the UK around 18 million adults have hearing loss or hear ringing or buzzing in their ears, which is called tinnitus. Many people wait a long time to be seen, partly because there are not enough audiologists - the specialists who test hearing and treat hearing problems.

The standard hearing test is called pure-tone audiometry. An audiologist plays quiet sounds at different pitches through headphones and the person presses a button each time they hear one. The test is accurate, but it takes 20 to 30 minutes to complete, and needs a trained audiologist for all of that time. For people with tinnitus and comorbidity it can be especially tiring and slow.

The research team has built a version of this test that uses artificial intelligence, called AI-PTA. Instead of following a fixed pattern, it chooses each sound based on the responses already given, which should mean fewer sound presentations are needed to find the same result. The audiologist stays with the person throughout and remains in charge of the test.

This study asks three questions.

1. Does AI-PTA give the same hearing results as the standard test?
2. Is it quicker?
3. And do patients and staff find it acceptable?

Who can participate?

Adults aged 18 or over who have been diagnosed with sensorineural hearing loss, either with or without tinnitus, and who are due to attend the Royal National ENT \& Eastman Dental Hospital in London. Participants need enough English to read and complete questionnaires and to be able to give informed consent. People who have or report hyperacusis (an unusual sensitivity to everyday sounds), an active ear infection, or recent ear surgery cannot take part.

What does the study involve?

People who are interested are sent information about two weeks before a hospital appointment they already have. Those who decide to take part come in about 30 minutes early, meet a research audiologist, discuss the study, and if happy to take part, sign a consent form. They fill in a short questionnaire about their hearing health.

They then have two hearing tests at that visit: the standard test, which is part of their normal care, and the AI-PTA test. Half of the participants have the standard test first and half have AI-PTA first, so that the order does not affect the results.

They come back within a week for a shorter appointment, about 40 minutes, to repeat the AI-PTA test. This shows whether it gives the same response twice. They also fill in a questionnaire about what they think of using artificial intelligence in healthcare. That is the end of taking part, though participants are also invited to join an optional group discussion about their opinions on AI in healthcare later on.

What are the possible benefits and risks of participating?

There is no direct benefit to taking part. The results will help decide whether tests like this can shorten waiting times for hearing assessments in the NHS.

The risks are small. Both tests use the same clinical equipment at the same safe sound levels that ordinary hearing tests use, and a qualified clinical audiologist is present throughout and can stop at any point. The main cost to participants is time: about 45 minutes extra at the first appointment and a second visit of about 40 minutes. Some people find hearing tests tiring, and people with tinnitus sometimes notice their tinnitus more during or after a hearing test. Taking part is voluntary, and choosing not to take part, or stopping at any time, will not affect anyone's care.

Where is the study run from?

Royal National ENT and Eastman Dental Hospitals in London which is part of University College London Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, and University College London.

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for?

The study was approved in August 2026 and the first participant took part in September 2026. It is expected to run for 12 months, finishing in August 2027.

Who is funding the study?

The British Society of Otology (part of ENT UK), and the National Institute for Health and Care Research University College London Hospitals Biomedical Research Centre.

Who is the main contact?

Dr Roulla Katiri, uclh.ahead@nhs.net
primary_outcomes: Agreement between hearing thresholds measured by AI-PTA and by Standard PTA
Number of tone presentations, by procedure
title: Comparing an AI-driven Hearing Test With the Standard Hearing Test in Adults With Hearing Loss and Tinnitus

brief_summary:
PROJECT SUMMARY Cholesteatoma is a serious otological condition that remains a serious problem and poses a great challenge to otolaryngologists around the globe. If it is left undetected and untreated, a cholesteatoma may cause serious complications e.g temporal bone resorption and cranial complications, with a tendency to erode surrounding bone, ear ossicles, fallopian canal of facial nerve, bony labyrinth, or intracranial cavity resulting in different grades of hearing loss, facial paralysis, vertigo or intracranial complications. The main management of cholesteatoma is complete surgical excision of cholesteatoma which is done traditionally under the microscope. The main problem in the management of cholesteatoma is recidivism either in the form of residual disease or recurrence. These limitations can be defeated with the complimentary help of the endoscope, which allows visualization of these hidden areas. In recent years the use of otoendoscope either exclusively or as an adjunct to the microscope is gaining popularity in the surgical management of cholesteatoma. The main benefit of this combination is the identification of remnant cholesteatoma and to prevent its recurrence.

Randomized Controlled trials will be conducted at the Department of ENT, Shaikh Zayed Hospital, Lahore for 1 year. The sample size of 30 cases; 15 cases in each group will be included through Non-probability consecutive sampling. Then eligible candidates will be divided into two groups based on random allocation (lottery method) i.e. group A will be cholesteatoma cases who will be having Microscopic mastoidectomy (either CWU or CWD) without check-endoscopy. And group B will be cholesteatoma cases who will be having Microscopic mastoidectomy (either CWU or CWD) followed by check-endoscopy in the same surgical session. All the cases will be operated under general anesthesia by the same consultant otolaryngolist having at least 4 years residency experience with the researcher as assistant. In Group B cases, after completing the excision of cholesteatoma with Microscopic Mastoidectomy, check endoscopy will be performed to visualize the concealed areas in the middle ear i.e sinus tympani, anterior epitympanum, protympanum, retrotympanum, and presence or absence of residual cholesteatoma will be recorded according to the site. If a residual cholesteatoma is found by the endoscope, its site will be noted then it will be removed in the same session. After surgery, patients will be discharged after 24-72 hours of post-Op care and will be followed-up in OPD for 6 months at 1st month, 3rd month, \& 6th month intervals. During follow-up visits, patients will be examined under the microscope for the condition of the middle ear cavity and mastoid cavity i.e. presence or absence of any ear discharge or visible cholesteatoma. All this information will be recorded on Performa (attached) and enter into SPSS version 23. Both groups will be compared for the presence of residual cholesteatoma and recurrence of cholesteatoma through cross-tabulation.

The study will help us to measure the role of check endoscopy as an adjunct to Microscopic Cholesteatoma Surgery, in terms of identifying the residual cholesteatoma and measuring the rate of cholesteatoma recurrence afterwards. This will be an addition to the local scientific data regarding cholesteatoma management within our demographic variables. As a result, it will be helpful for us to utilize this knowledge to improve our practice and combined approach towards Microscopic Mastoidectomy for Cholesteatoma Excision.
conditions: Identification of Residual Cholesteatoma After Microscopic Mastoidectomy With and Without Check Endocscopy
interventions: Mastoidectomy with and without check endoscopy for cholesteatoma surgery

brief_summary:
Most patients resuscitated from out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) remain comatose on hospital admission and are routinely managed with continuous sedation. Sedation facilitates temperature control, but deep and prolonged sedation is associated with longer mechanical ventilation, delirium, infections and delayed awakening. It is unknown whether minimizing sedation increases secondary hypoxic-ischemic brain injury.

This single-centre, open-label, randomized non-inferiority trial will compare a minimal sedation strategy (no continuous sedation) with standard continuous sedation in 100 comatose adults after OHCA. The primary outcome is serum neuron-specific enolase (NSE) 72 hours after return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC). Secondary outcomes include in-hospital mortality, neurological outcome at discharge, duration of mechanical ventilation and length of ICU stay.
title: Minimal Sedation Versus Standard Continuous Sedation After Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest

brief_summary:
This study will examine whether a 12-week Ayres Sensory Integration (ASI)-based physiotherapy program can improve motor skills and daily functioning in young children with cerebral palsy. Thirty children aged 3 to 6 years who meet the study criteria will be assigned to an intervention group or a control group.

Children in the intervention group will receive 36 sessions of ASI-based physiotherapy over 12 weeks. Each session will last 60 minutes and will be provided by a physiotherapist certified in ASI. Children in the control group will continue their usual physiotherapy and rehabilitation and will not receive additional ASI as part of the study.

Children will be assessed before and after the 12-week study period. Assessments will include measures of motor skills, development, daily activities, sensory processing, and progress toward individual goals. The Evaluation in Ayres Sensory Integration (EASI) will be completed before the intervention only. Assessments will be carried out in a clinical setting by an assessor who is independent of the therapists providing the intervention.
primary_outcomes: Peabody Developmental Motor Scales, Second Edition (PDMS-2)
title: Ayres Sensory Integration Intervention for Children With Cerebral Palsy

brief_summary:
Small cell lung cancer (SCLC) is a type of lung cancer that accounts for approximately 15-17% of all lung cancers. It is characterized by aggressive and rapid growth and early spread to distant sites. Extensive stage-small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC) includes cases where disease has spread beyond one side of the chest. The purpose of this study is to assess safety and efficacy of ABBV-706 in combination with tarlatamab and atezolizumab in participants with ES-SCLC.

ABBV-706 is an investigational drug being developed for the treatment of ESSCLC. This is an open-label study, meaning participants and doctors know which treatment is being given. Participants are placed into 1 of 2 treatment arms. Each arm receives a different dose of ABBV-706 in combination with tarlatamab and atezolizumab. Adult participants with a diagnosis of extensive stage-small cell lung cancer will be enrolled. Around 80 participants will be enrolled in the study at approximately 25 sites worldwide.

Participants will receive intravenous (IV) doses of ABBV-706 in combination with IV atezolizumab and IV tarlatamab. The study will run for a duration of approximately 62 months.

There may be higher treatment burden for participants in this trial compared to their standard of care due to study procedures. Participants will attend regular visits during the study at a hospital or clinic. The effects of the treatment will be checked by medical assessments, blood tests, imaging scans, checking for side effects and completing questionnaires.
primary_outcomes: Objective Response (OR) measured by overall response rate (ORR) Based on Blinded Independent Central Review (BICR) Assessment Per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) Version 1.1
Number of Participants with Adverse Events (AEs)
title: A Study to Assess Adverse Events and Change in Disease Activity of Intravenous (IV) ABBV-706 in Combination With Tarlatamab and Atezolizumab in Adult Participants With Extensive Stage-Small Cell Lung Cancer

brief_summary: MELODY is a prospective, single-arm phase II study introducing routine liquid-biopsy next-generation sequencing for patients with advanced or unresectable breast cancer in Ireland. The study will characterise genomic alterations detected in plasma and tumour tissue, assess concordance and clinical actionability, and evaluate clinical, operational, economic, patient-reported and exploratory translational outcomes.
title: Mapping the Enhanced Landscape of Advanced Breast Cancer fOr DYnamic Treatment Approaches

brief_summary: This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness and scalability of a clinical management model based on the use of Diagnosis-Related Groups (DRGs) in a high-complexity hospital in Chile. A quasi-experimental design will be used, comparing efficiency and quality indicators between patients managed under the new DRG model versus usual care.
primary_outcomes: Clinical Efficiency - Average Length of Stay
title: Evaluation of a DRG-Based Clinical Management Model in a High-Complexity Chilean Hospital

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to learn whether adjusting abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) size for body size helps distinguish ruptured from intact aneurysms better than maximum aneurysm diameter alone. The study will evaluate the Aortic Size Index, which adjusts aneurysm diameter for body surface area, and the Aortic Height Index, which adjusts aneurysm diameter for height.

The main questions are:

1. Do the Aortic Size Index or Aortic Height Index distinguish ruptured from intact AAAs better than maximum aneurysm diameter alone?
2. What proportion of ruptured AAAs occur below the diameter thresholds of 55 millimeters for men and 50 millimeters for women?
3. Do the findings vary according to sex, participating country, or participating center?

The study will include adults presenting with a ruptured infrarenal AAA and adults with an intact infrarenal AAA undergoing open surgical or endovascular repair. Participants will not receive an experimental treatment. Researchers will use computed tomography scans obtained before surgical or endovascular treatment and available height and weight measurements. No additional computed tomography scans will be required for the study.

Researchers will also collect clinical, operative, and mortality information. Vital status will be recorded during the repair procedure, during the index hospitalization, and at 30-day follow-up. For participants who undergo AAA repair, the 30-day period will begin on the date of repair. For participants who do not undergo repair, it will begin on the date of the index clinical presentation. The 30-day assessment will use institutional medical records or telephone contact when necessary.
primary_outcomes: Difference in Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve Between Aortic Size Index and Maximum Aneurysm Diameter
Difference in Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve Between Aortic Height Index and Maximum Aneurysm Diameter
title: Aortic Size and Height Indices in Abdominal Aortic Aneurysms

brief_summary: The aim of this study is to investigate the effect of transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) added to manual therapy on pain, autonomic nervous system function, and illness perception in female patients diagnosed with fibromyalgia, using a randomized sham-controlled design.
interventions: Sham Transcutaneous Auricular Vagus Nerve Stimulation (Sham taVNS)
title: Effects of Adding Vagal Neuromodulation to Manual Therapy in Women With Fibromyalgia

brief_summary: Patients with indeterminate lung nodules often face a choice between continued CT surveillance and invasive investigation. This trial compares management with or without access to an AI report that matches nodules across real serial CT scans, measures change, and estimates validated malignancy or invasiveness risks. The principal question is whether offering the report reduces lung resections that yield benign pathology over 24 months. Diagnostic delay, cancer stage, treatment opportunity, complications, and longer-term cancer outcomes are also assessed.
interventions: AI-Assisted Longitudinal CT Assessment and Pulmonary Nodule Management
lead_sponsor: Union Hospital, Tongji Medical College, Huazhong University of Science and Technology
primary_outcomes: Lung Resection Yielding Benign Pathology Within 24 Months
title: Longitudinal AI-Assisted Management of Indeterminate Pulmonary Nodules

brief_summary:
he IRON-TAVI trial is a prospective, randomized, multicenter study evaluating whether a multidomain rehabilitation program can improve outcomes in older patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation for severe symptomatic aortic stenosis.

The study will enroll approximately 450 patients aged 75 years or older who have reduced physical performance and/or impaired nutritional status. Participants will be randomly assigned in a one-to-one ratio to either standard care or a multidomain intervention in addition to standard care.

The multidomain intervention includes a personalized exercise program, combining supervised sessions before and after transcatheter aortic valve implantation with home-based exercises, together with individualized nutritional counseling and oral supplementation containing protein and iron. The intervention starts before the valve procedure and continues during the first three months after the procedure.

The study will assess whether this strategy improves clinical outcomes, physical performance, nutritional status, and quality of life compared with standard care alone. The main outcome will be the occurrence within one year of death from any cause, stroke, or hospital readmission for cardiovascular causes.
interventions: Oral Protein and Iron Nutritional Supplementation
primary_outcomes: Time to First All-Cause Death, Stroke, or Hospital Readmission for Cardiovascular Causes
title: Exercise and Diet Supplements for Older Patients Undergoing TAVI: the IRON-TAVI Trial

brief_summary: Survivors of subarachnoid haemorrhage (SAH) frequently experience cognitive, psychological, physical and social sequelae, but no French-language instrument covers all these dimensions. The SAHOT (Subarachnoid Haemorrhage Outcome Tool), developed and validated in English, is a SAH-specific patient-reported outcome measure. This prospective single-centre cohort study aims to validate the French translation of the SAHOT in adult patients seen at a follow-up consultation within 12 months after a SAH of any aetiology. The primary objective is to assess the internal consistency of the French SAHOT. Seventy patients will be included; accompanying relatives may also be included to complete a proxy version of the questionnaire.
primary_outcomes: Internal consistency of the French version of the SAHOT
title: French Validation of the SAHOT Outcome Scale After Subarachnoid Haemorrhage

brief_summary: Adults hospitalized with pneumonia who need new or increased oxygen support or have defined immunocompromise will be assigned to usual care with or without access to a CT-based AI report. The report summarizes likely pathogen classes, lung involvement, and short-term deterioration risk. Clinicians review the report alongside images and clinical evidence and retain responsibility for testing and treatment. The trial asks whether AI-assisted care reduces death or new invasive respiratory or circulatory support within 28 days. Patients are followed after discharge through day 90.
interventions: CT-Based AI Decision Support for Pneumonia
lead_sponsor: Union Hospital, Tongji Medical College, Huazhong University of Science and Technology
primary_outcomes: Death or New Invasive Respiratory or Circulatory Support Within 28 Days
title: A Multicenter Randomized Trial of CT-Based AI Decision Support for Early Pneumonia Care

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if KM-023 is safe and well tolerated in adults with Pachyonychia Congenita (PC). The study will also explore whether KM-023 may help reduce pain, improve mobility, and lessen the impact of PC on participants' daily lives.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

What medical problems or side effects do participants experience when taking KM-023? Does KM-023 improve participants' ability to walk and perform physical activities? Does KM-023 reduce pain, especially pain in the soles of the feet? How does KM-023 affect the severity and impact of PC symptoms?

Researchers will evaluate changes during treatment compared with participants' condition at the start of the study.

The study will include 10 adults with genetically confirmed PC who have visible painful calluses on the soles of their feet. All participants will receive KM-023; there is no placebo group.

Each participant will be involved in the study for up to 170 days, including screening, treatment, and follow-up.
