brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to investigate whether lifestyle factors can alter gut barrier integrity and whether disruptions of the gut barrier can trigger systemic and tissue-specific inflammation. Twenty participants will undergo 14 days of fast-food overfeeding. Gut barrier function will be assessed before and after the intervention, alongside a wide palette of imaging techniques and biological analyses to characterize inflammatory status.
title: Changes in Intestinal Permeability and Systemic Inflammation Following Fast Food Overfeeding.

brief_summary:
Spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) is a rare neuromuscular disease causing progressive muscle weakness related to degeneration of motor neurons. With the arrival of new treatments, the natural history of SMA is changing significantly, and treatments in adults have been associated with disease stabilization and a reduction in fatigue. However, functional assessment of adult patients remains difficult: their motor performance is highly fluctuating and hospital-based tests incompletely capture these daily variations.

Wearable devices, such as Syde®, now allow continuous monitoring in real life. The Syde® device, already used in Duchenne muscular dystrophy, provides digital measures describing gait and overall motor activity. However, no fully validated digital measure currently exists in adults with SMA.

The SMAdult study aims to address this gap through a precise, longitudinal, and fully decentralized follow-up of adults with SMA.

Objectives

* Primary objectives: Evaluation of the usability, reliability, and optimal use of a wearable device (Syde®) to monitor motor evolution in adults with SMA.
* Secondary objectives: To study the clinical validity of digital biomarkers by correlating them with functional scales (HFMSE, RULM). To determine the ability of digital measures to discriminate patients according to SMN2 copy number, phenotype, or treatments received. To follow the longitudinal evolution of Syde® measures in order to identify decline, stabilization, or improvement. To analyze subjective perception of progression through validated questionnaires and interviews.

Methodology Study type Academic, monocentric, prospective, fully decentralized study. Total duration: 36 months (24 months of inclusion, and between 12 and 30 months of follow-up).

Target population 60 adults aged over 15 years with genetically confirmed SMA. With a minimum of 20 ambulatory patients and 20 non-ambulatory patients.

On stable treatment for more than 1 year.

Procedure:

* Remote inclusion, with electronic consent via electronic software such as DocuSign.
* Follow-up every 6 months by questionnaire and videoconference.
* Use of a connected home device: Syde® (gait sensor).
* No hospital visits required.
* Collection of motor data, routine clinical information, validated questionnaires on swallowing, CGI questionnaire improvement and comparison.

Benefits and risks

* Direct benefits: limited but potential (enhanced monitoring).
* Collective benefits: improvement of monitoring tools and outcome measures in adult SMA patients.
* Risks: very low; use of non-invasive sensors with no known side effects.

Ethical aspects

* Compliance with GCP and GDPR.
* Oral and electronic informed consent.
* Pseudonymized data, analyzed by approved partners (SYSNAV).
* No compensation planned; no travel required.
* Insurance provided by the sponsor
title: SMAdult - Monitoring of Movement on Spinal Muscular Atrophy

brief_summary:
Children with lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI) are still often prescribed antibiotics in ways that depart from national guidelines. Acute viral bronchitis is treated with antibiotics although none are needed, and community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) is often treated with a second-choice antibiotic, most often a macrolide, instead of first-line amoxicillin. In the Terveystalo network in Finland, about one third of bronchitis visits and one fifth of CAP visits in 2014 to 2020 led to an antibiotic prescription, and macrolides were the most commonly prescribed agent for bronchitis.

PRACTICE-LRTI is a nationwide quality-improvement and implementation study in which all clinics of the network receive a multimodal antimicrobial stewardship programme aimed at prescribing clinicians (paediatricians, general practitioners, ear, nose and throat specialists and other physicians). The programme combines (1) a concise local version of the Finnish Current Care Guideline for paediatric LRTI; (2) education for physicians and caregivers (printed and intranet materials, videos, webinars, unit-level meetings, online courses and commitment posters); (3) light-touch electronic health record reminders and a one-click supportive-care order set; and (4) a real-time prescribing dashboard with a structured feedback cascade that escalates over three years from network-wide progress reports to targeted outreach to non-improving units and, finally, personalised letters and phone calls to persistently non-concordant prescribers. A one-page guide prompts clinicians to question unverified penicillin-allergy labels.

The programme is delivered to the whole network at the same time, so no clinics are randomised to a control condition. Instead, prescribing is followed as a monthly time series from 2014 onward, and the change after each of three prespecified intervention steps is estimated by segmented regression against the projected pre-intervention trend. The co-primary outcomes are the proportion of acute bronchitis episodes in which a systemic antibiotic is prescribed and the proportion of antibiotic-treated outpatient CAP episodes in which a non-first-line agent is prescribed. The co-primary outcomes are assessed at Month 36 after launch; their Month 12 and Month 48 assessments are secondary outcomes. Other secondary outcomes include first-line amoxicillin and macrolide use, 5-day treatment duration, variation between units and physicians, diagnostic testing, first-line prescribing in children with a penicillin-allergy label, and intervention cost. Safety is monitored through 14-day respiratory revisits, hospital referrals and hospitalisations. The active intervention lasts 3 years and is followed by 1 year of follow-up to assess durability.

This is a quality-improvement and implementation study embedded in routine care, not a trial of a treatment. The intervention is directed at physicians; no child is recruited, contacted or examined outside routine care, and all outcome data come from the network's electronic health record.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of acute bronchitis episodes with a systemic antibiotic prescription
Proportion of antibiotic-treated outpatient community-acquired pneumonia episodes with a non-first-line antibiotic
title: Multimodal Stewardship Programme to Improve Antibiotic Prescribing for Children With Lower Respiratory Tract Infections

brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to reveal the effectiveness and safety of ultrasound-guided pharmacopuncture for patients with tension-type headache caused by a traffic accident. It is a pragmatic clinical study to confirm the comparative effectiveness by comparing the strategy of combining ultrasound-guided pharmacopuncture in parallel with the strategy of treating with integrative Korean medicine treatment, which is an existing treatment method.
title: Efficacy and Safety of Ultrasound-Guided Pharmacopuncture as an Adjunctive Therapy in Inpatients With Post-Traffic Accident Tension-Type Headache

brief_summary:
This randomized clinical trial aims to evaluate the clinical and immunological effects of locally delivered Spirulina gel as an adjunct to scaling and root planing (SRP) in patients with Stage II, Grade B periodontitis. The study will include 20 male and female participants aged 25-40 years who will be randomly allocated into two groups.

The main questions are whether the addition of Spirulina gel to SRP improves periodontal clinical parameters, particularly probing pocket depth (PPD) and clinical attachment level (CAL), and whether it reduces the levels of interleukin-1β (IL-1β) and tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α) in gingival crevicular fluid (GCF).

Participants in Group A will receive SRP alone, while participants in Group B will receive SRP followed by local application of Spirulina gel into selected periodontal pockets. All participants will undergo periodontal assessments at baseline and 6 months after treatment. Clinical evaluations will include plaque index, gingival index, PPD, and CAL. GCF samples will be collected at baseline, 15 days and 6 months, analyzed using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) to measure IL-1β and TNF-α levels.

The findings will help determine whether adjunctive local application of Spirulina gel provides additional clinical and immunological benefits compared with SRP alone in the management of Stage II, Grade B periodontitis.
interventions: spirulina gel exracted by 1.5% calcium chloride (CaCl2) aqueous solution.
lead_sponsor: Misr University for Science and Technology
title: Spirulina Gel in the Treatment of Periodontitis

brief_summary: This will be a prospective, randomized, controlled non-inferiority trial comparing the efficacy of Iheezo versus subconjunctival 2% lidocaine in reducing intravitreal injection pain scores up to 24 hours after injection.
title: Comparing Intravitreal Injection Pain Scores Using Iheezo (Chloroprocaine Hcl Ophthalmic Gel 3%) Versus Subconjunctival Lidocaine (2%): A Randomized, Controlled Trial

brief_summary:
Cervical radiculopathy caused by cervical disc herniation or foraminal stenosis is a common condition that may result in upper limb pain, sensory disturbances, and motor deficits. Anterior cervical discectomy and fusion (ACDF) is an established surgical treatment, providing effective nerve root decompression. However, this procedure requires intervertebral fusion and may be associated with complications such as pseudarthrosis, adjacent segment degeneration, dysphagia, and recurrent laryngeal nerve injury.

Uniportal endoscopic posterior cervical foraminotomy (UEPCF) is a minimally invasive alternative that enables direct nerve root decompression without intervertebral fusion. This technique may preserve cervical segmental mobility and reduce approach-related morbidity. Nevertheless, prospective randomized evidence comparing uniportal endoscopic posterior cervical foraminotomy with ACDF remains limited.

ENDOFOR is a prospective, single-center, randomized, open-label, controlled non-inferiority trial designed to assess whether uniportal endoscopic posterior cervical foraminotomy is non-inferior to ACDF in reducing upper limb radicular pain three months after surgery.

A total of 46 patients with cervical radiculopathy related to cervical disc herniation or foraminal stenosis will be randomized in a 1:1 ratio to undergo either uniportal endoscopic posterior cervical foraminotomy or ACDF.

The primary outcome is upper limb radicular pain intensity at three months after surgery, assessed using a patient-reported 0-10 pain scale and adjusted for baseline pain intensity. Secondary outcomes include cervical pain, functional disability, postoperative complications, operative duration, length of hospital stay, adjacent segment disc degeneration, and fusion status.

Patients will be followed for 12 months after surgery. The study aims to provide prospective randomized evidence regarding the effectiveness and safety of a minimally invasive surgical alternative to cervical fusion.
primary_outcomes: Upper Limb Radicular Pain Intensity at 3 Months After Surgery
title: Endoscopic Posterior Cervical Foraminotomy Versus Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion for Cervical Radiculopathy

brief_summary: Depressive disorders are highly prevalent among older adults with asthma and are associated with poor asthma outcomes. The overall objective of this study is to integrate an asthma self-management support program that the research team previously developed with cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) for adherence and depression for older adults with uncontrolled asthma and a comorbid depressive disorder. The research team will conduct a pilot randomized controlled trial to assess the feasibility and preliminary impact of the intervention on asthma and depression outcomes.
lead_sponsor: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai
title: R34 Asthma Depression

brief_summary: Fibroblast Growth Factor 19 (FGF-19) is an intestinal hormone secreted in the post-prandial state, whose primary role is to inhibit bile acid synthesis in the liver. It is expressed by the FXR (Farnesoid X receptor) nuclear receptor in the enterocytes of the ileum, which is activated by specific bile acids metabolized in the gut microbiota. It was demonstrated that treatment with FGF-19 induces myofiber hypertrophy in vitro and increases muscle strength and mass in mice model of sarcopenia. Sarcopenia and the commonly associated physical frailty, are age-related syndromes associated with adverse events (such as falls and fractures, mobility disability) and increased mortality. Currently, there is no drug treatment that has been proven effective to counteract those syndromes and standard care consists in non-pharmacological interventions (exercise and nutrition) whose implementation remains complex due to several barriers. Moreover, the anabolic resistance underlying sarcopenia hampers the exercise-induced response on muscle mass and the level of evidence for this outcome remains poor-to-moderate. Thus, FGF-19 could be considered as a new regulator of skeletal muscle in elderly living with sarcopenia/frailty but there are, to date, only few data available in the literature. First and foremost, it is crucial to understand the relationship between postprandial FGF-19 and muscle which has not been characterized yet. Preliminary data suggest an inverse relationship between FGF-19 and physical function (OR= 0.33 \[0.15;0.7\] for the highest tertile of FGF-19) that persisted only in the cluster of frail individuals (OR= 0.19 \[0.05;0.65\]. Mechanistically, this suggests a positive feedback loop of the bile acids-gut-microbiota-FGF-19 in the presence of frailty/sarcopenia hence indicating that FGF-19 may be a novel biomarker of this condition.
primary_outcomes: Area Under Curve (AUC) of plasmatic post-prandial FGF-19 level
title: PROfiles of FGF-19 Post-prandial Secretion in Older Adults With Frailty and Without Frailty

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study (retrospective cohort study) is to determine whether DNA methylation status in archived cervical cytology samples can predict regression, persistence, or progression of high-grade cervical dysplasia (HSIL/CIN2-3) in women who have previously undergone clinical management and follow-up.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

Can methylation status in archived cervical cytology samples predict histologic regression of HSIL (CIN2/3)? Does the addition of clinical factors, screening history, smoking status, and HPV genotype improve the predictive ability of methylation markers for disease regression, persistence, or progression?

Researchers will compare:

Women whose lesions regressed with women whose lesions persisted or progressed. Methylation-positive and methylation-negative samples to assess whether methylation status is associated with subsequent clinical outcomes.

Participants will:

Be identified retrospectively from women aged 23 to 70 years who were previously diagnosed with HSIL/CIN2-3 and managed according to routine clinical practice.

Have archived cervical cytology samples retrieved from biobanks for DNA methylation analysis.

Contribute existing clinical, cytological, histological, and HPV data collected during routine care.

Contribute existing follow-up data from medical records, including outcomes such as regression, persistence, progression, and treatment results.

No additional interventions, testing, or follow-up visits will be performed as part of the study; all analyses will be based on retrospectively collected biological samples and clinical data.
conditions: HSIL, High Grade Squamous Intraepithelial Lesion
primary_outcomes: Methylation status (alone) as a predictor of histologic regression of cervical biopsy HSIL (CIN2/3) in cone specimen (Part A) and as a predictor of histologic regression of cervical HSIL (CIN2) within 24 months of follow-up
title: Predictive Biomarkers for Precision Management of Pre-cancerous Cervical Neoplasia

brief_summary:
This study evaluates whether placing 0.2% chlorhexidine gel into the tooth socket after lower wisdom tooth surgery improves gum healing, reduces bacteria on surgical stitches, and decreases postoperative pain, swelling, and difficulty opening the mouth.

Participants require surgical removal of both lower wisdom teeth. Each participant receives both treatments in separate operations at least four weeks apart. One side is randomly assigned to receive 1 mL of chlorhexidine gel before the wound is stitched closed. The other side receives no gel and serves as the comparison. Both sides receive the same standard postoperative care.

Pain and self-reported swelling are assessed on days 1, 3, and 7 after each operation. Facial swelling, mouth opening, and gum healing are assessed on days 3 and 7. A small sample of the surgical stitch is collected on day 7 to measure bacterial growth. Participants are also monitored for dry socket during the seven-day follow-up period.
lead_sponsor: University of Medicine and Pharmacy at Ho Chi Minh City
title: Chlorhexidine Gel After Third Molar Surgery

brief_summary:
This randomized clinical trial aims to compare the recurrence of bacterial vaginosis (BV) in women receiving probiotics alongside antibiotic treatment versus women receiving antibiotic treatment alone. Bacterial vaginosis is a common vaginal condition that can recur after successful treatment.

The main question this study aims to answer is:

\- Does adding probiotics to standard antibiotic treatment reduce the recurrence of bacterial vaginosis compared with antibiotic treatment alone?

The study will include 70 non-pregnant women aged 20-45 years diagnosed with recurrent bacterial vaginosis. All participants will initially receive metronidazole to treat the current episode. After successful treatment is confirmed, participants will be randomly assigned to one of two groups:

* Group A: Probiotic capsules containing Lactobacillus plantarum, Lactobacillus rhamnosus, and Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis, followed by monthly maintenance dosing for four months.
* Group B: Placebo capsules, followed by the same monthly maintenance schedule.

Participants will undergo monthly vaginal examinations for four months to assess whether bacterial vaginosis recurs. Recurrence will be diagnosed using Amsel's criteria, which include assessment of vaginal discharge, vaginal pH, clue cells on microscopy, and a characteristic fishy odor test.

The researchers will compare the frequency of bacterial vaginosis recurrence between the two groups to determine whether adjunctive probiotic treatment reduces recurrence.
title: Probiotics as an Adjunct to Antibiotics for Recurrent Bacterial Vaginosis

brief_summary:
This study is a multicenter, open-label, single-arm extension study to evaluate the safety and efficacy of long-term administration of Inpegsomatropin Injection in participants with Idiopathic Short Stature (ISS) who have completed Phase Ⅲ clinical trials.

Upon completion of the Phase Ⅲ clinical study, participants may enter the extension-phase baseline assessment period after the participant and their guardian provide informed consent, based on the willingness of the participant and guardian as well as the investigator's comprehensive assessment of the benefit-risk profile for the participant's continued participation in this study. Participants who meet all inclusion criteria and do not meet any exclusion criteria will proceed to the extension-phase treatment period to receive continued treatment with Inpegsomatropin Injection. Upon completion of the treatment period, participants will enter the final-height follow-up period, during which growth and development status, medication exposure and safety will be followed up via outpatient visits. This study aims to observe the long-term safety and efficacy of the investigational product.
primary_outcomes: Safety: number of participants with adverse event (AE), serious adverse events (SAE) and clinically significant examination results.
title: A Clinical Study of Long-Term Administration of Inpegsomatropin Injection in Participants With Idiopathic Short Stature Who Have Completed Phase Ⅲ Clinical Trials

brief_summary:
Dental anxiety is common among children and may make dental treatment more difficult. This study aims to compare three non-pharmacological behavior guidance techniques for reducing dental anxiety and improving cooperation during invasive fissure sealant treatment in children aged 6-10 years.

Children who require an invasive fissure sealant on a mandibular first molar and meet the study eligibility criteria will be included. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of three groups. The first group will watch a 1.5-2-minute Point-of-View (POV) video showing the dental examination and treatment process from a child's perspective before the dental procedure. The second group will use virtual reality (VR) glasses during the procedure and watch age-appropriate animation or cartoon content as an active distraction technique. The control group will receive the standard Tell-Show-Do behavior guidance technique.

Dental anxiety, behavior, physiological responses, and pain will be assessed using the Children's Fear Survey Schedule-Dental Subscale (CFSS-DS), Facial Image Scale (FIS), Frankl Behavior Rating Scale, pulse rate, oxygen saturation, and Wong-Baker FACES Pain Rating Scale. A post-intervention satisfaction and experience questionnaire will also be administered to assess the children's experiences with the behavior guidance techniques.

The study is expected to provide comparative evidence regarding the effectiveness of POV video modeling and VR distraction compared with the standard Tell-Show-Do technique in managing dental anxiety and improving children's cooperation during dental treatment.
title: Virtual Reality and Point-of-View Video Modeling for Dental Anxiety in Children

brief_summary: This post-marketing surveillance aims to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of zastaprazan citrate administered in Korean patients receiving the drug in accordance with the approved prescribing information.

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to investigate whether personalized multi-electrode transcutaneous spinal cord stimulation (tSCS), guided by machine learning (ML) and combined with gait training, can improve walking function in people with spinal cord injury or stroke compared with single-electrode tonic stimulation combined with the same training.

tSCS is a non-invasive technique that delivers electrical pulses through electrodes placed on the skin over the spine to modulate spinal neural circuits, facilitate the recruitment of lower-limb muscles, and support the recovery of voluntary movements. Conventional tSCS typically uses a single stimulation electrode, which may limit selective recruitment of different muscle groups. This study investigates a personalized multi-electrode approach to selectively recruit specific lower-limb muscle groups and deliver stimulation at appropriate phases of the gait cycle, with the aim of improving walking function.

The main questions this study aims to answer are:

1. How do electrode positions and stimulation intensities affect selective muscle recruitment, and how do responses vary between participants and days?
2. Can ML-based optimization identify stimulation settings with selectivity comparable to complete mapping of muscle responses, using fewer tests and less time?
3. Does personalized multi-electrode stimulation, synchronized with specific gait phases, improve walking function more than single-electrode tonic stimulation when both are combined with gait training?

The study includes 24 participants (14 with spinal cord injury and 10 with stroke) and consists of two stages.

Stage 1 - Characterization of tSCS Selectivity and Stimulation Optimization

All participants complete two experimental sessions while lying down. Researchers compare muscle responses to stimulation at a central electrode and at multiple spinal electrode locations. Electrical responses in the leg muscles are recorded using surface electromyography (EMG), and spinal reflexes are assessed using paired electrical pulses.

By systematically testing electrode positions and stimulation intensities, researchers build a map of which leg muscles respond to each setting (stimulation landscape). They assess the selective recruitment of different muscle groups, compare stimulation locations, and examine differences between participants and across the two sessions. They also test whether ML-based optimization can find similarly selective settings more efficiently than the complete mapping procedure.

Stage 2 - tSCS Combined With Gait Training

Participants are randomly assigned to one of two groups: single-electrode or multi-electrode tSCS, both combined with gait training. During spinal cord injury recruitment, the randomization procedure was adapted to better balance participants with different baseline walking abilities across groups.

Before each training session, participants lie down for an individualized calibration. An ML-based optimization method uses recorded muscle responses to select electrode positions and stimulation intensities for the subsequent walking session.

During walking, the single-electrode group receives continuous stimulation through one selected electrode. In the multi-electrode group, stimulation is delivered through electrodes selected to preferentially recruit different target muscle groups. A predefined walking-cycle model determines when stimulation should be delivered, based on gait phases detected in real time by wearable movement sensors.

Both groups complete 20 supervised training sessions over four weeks, including 30 minutes of treadmill walking per session. Walking speed is selected according to each participant's comfort and ability, with therapist adjustments, body-weight support, and physical assistance as needed.

Clinical and functional assessments are conducted before the intervention (T0), after the 20 sessions (T1), and at a 30-day follow-up (T2). They examine walking performance, muscle strength, spasticity, balance, and mobility. Additional measurements assess muscle activation, brain activity, and biological markers associated with neuroplasticity. The follow-up assesses whether changes are maintained after training.
lead_sponsor: University of Sao Paulo General Hospital
primary_outcomes: Change in Walking Speed Assessed by the 10-Meter Walk Test (10MWT)
title: AI-Guided Multi-Electrode Transcutaneous Spinal Cord Stimulation for Gait Rehabilitation in People With Spinal Cord Injury or Stroke

brief_summary: This is a single-group, open-label, uncontrolled clinical trial designed to evaluate the effects of Adrenal Adapt, a commercially available dietary supplement, on sleep quality, daytime energy, stress resilience, and cognitive performance over a 12-week intervention period in 40 healthy adults aged 18-60.
conditions: Reduces Afternoon Energy Crashes and Midday Fatigue
Improves Overall Sleep Quality and Restorative Sleep
Helps People Fall Asleep Faster and Wake Less During the Night
Improves the Body's Resilience and Recovery in Response to Everyday Stress
Reduces Perceived Stress and Feelings of Overwhelm
Improves Cognitive Performance, Mental Clarity, and Calm Focus Throughout the Day
Provides Calm, Steady Energy Without Jitteriness or Overstimulation
Reduces Reliance on Caffeine for Daily Energy
title: A Clinical Trial to Evaluate the Effects of Adrenal Adapt on Sleep Quality, Daytime Energy, Stress Resilience, and Cognitive Performance.

brief_summary:
Title Clinical Outcomes of Stroke in MalIgnanCy (COSMIC). Aims To characterize acute ischemic stroke (AIS) and spontaneous non-traumatic intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) occurring in patients with current or previous malignancy; to define cancer-, stroke-, imaging-, treatment-, and laboratory-related phenotypes; and to quantify short- and medium-term neurological, vascular, bleeding, functional, and mortality outcomes.

Study design Multicenter, observational, prospective real-world registry. No study-mandated therapeutic intervention is assigned.

Setting Participating emergency departments, stroke units, neurology departments, neurocritical-care units, oncology/hematology services, and affiliated hospitals. Consecutive eligible cases should be entered at each site to reduce selection bias. Participation is restricted to centers that routinely apply an occult-malignancy screening protocol in patients with cryptogenic ischemic stroke, including at minimum blood testing and total-body CT with or without intravenous contrast, according to local clinical practice and contraindications.

Study population Adults (≥18 years) with imaging-confirmed AIS or spontaneous non-traumatic parenchymal ICH and a documented current or previous qualifying malignancy. Basal cell carcinoma and cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma are excluded as qualifying malignancies.

Enrollment period Index strokes occurring during the 2-year enrollment period beginning on the date of central ethics committee approval, with standardized follow-up at 90±14 days and 365±30 days.

Overall study duration Prospective enrollment will continue for 2 years from the date of central ethics committee approval. Each participant will undergo follow-up at 90±14 days and 365±30 days; therefore, overall study completion will occur after the final enrolled participant completes the 1-year follow-up window, followed by database cleaning and lock.

Primary objective To estimate the 1-year cumulative incidence of any recurrent stroke after the index event in patients with malignancy, overall and separately after index AIS and index ICH.

Primary endpoint Any recurrent stroke within 1 year, defined as recurrent ischemic stroke and/or new spontaneous non-traumatic ICH occurring after the index event. Hemorrhagic transformation of an ischemic infarct is not counted as recurrent ICH.

Key secondary endpoints All-cause mortality and vascular death; ordinal modified Rankin Scale (mRS) and functional dependency; recurrent AIS and recurrent ICH separately; myocardial infarction; venous thromboembolism (VTE); ISTH major extracranial bleeding; net adverse clinical events; seizures; atrial fibrillation detected after stroke (AFDAS); and time-varying cancer status/treatment.

Sample size No fixed hypothesis-driven sample size is imposed. COSMIC is an inclusive registry and participating sites will enroll all consecutive eligible patients. Precision and model complexity will be determined by the final number of patients and outcome events.

Statistical approach Descriptive analyses; time-to-event and cumulative incidence analyses, accounting for death as a competing event where appropriate; cause-specific Cox and/or Fine-Gray regression models; Kaplan-Meier and Cox proportional hazards analyses for mortality; ordinal regression for functional outcome (mRS); multivariable adjustment for clinically relevant covariates; center-clustered inference; and prespecified subgroup and exploratory analyses.

Funding No study-specific funding is assumed in this protocol version; any subsequent funding source will be disclosed in study documents and publications.
interventions: 1-year cumulative incidence of any recurrent stroke after the index event in patients with malignancy, overall and separately after index AIS and index ICH.
title: Clinical Outcomes of Stroke in MalIgnanCy

brief_summary: In this randomized, sham-controlled, two-group, parallel, single-session study, the investigators aim to identify EEG biomarkers associated with cerebellar transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) in patients with persistent post-concussion symptoms (PPCS). Cerebellar tDCS will be used to modulate brain network connectivity, which is known to be altered in PPCS. The study will include 38 participants, each completing a single session including EEG recordings before and after stimulation. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of two conditions: 1) active cerebellar tDCS, or 2) sham stimulation.By focusing on EEG functional connectivity and related signal metrics, this study aims to better understand the neural mechanisms of cerebellar tDCS and support the development of targeted interventions for patients with PPCS.
primary_outcomes: EEG Functional Connectivity in the Alpha Band (dwPLI)
title: Electroencephalography Markers of Brain Stimulation in Post-Concussion Patients

brief_summary: Many patients feel anxious while waiting to see a dermatologist, especially in clinics that diagnose and treat skin cancer. The purpose of this study was to learn whether spending 10 minutes before the visit in an exam room lit by a tabletop colored-light device, which patients control themselves, lowers anxiety compared with usual room lighting. Adult patients at one Stanford dermatology clinic were assigned by clinic week: during intervention weeks the device was on and patients could choose its color and brightness with a handheld remote; during control weeks the room had standard lighting. Patients answered short questionnaires about how they felt when they arrived and again after 10 minutes in the room.
title: Patient-Controlled Ambient Light to Reduce Pre-Visit Anxiety in Dermatology Patients

brief_summary: Knee replacements are the second most common surgery in Canada. Most patients recover very well but research consistently shows that 1 in 5 patients still have pain many months after surgery. Doctors often prescribe opioid medications for pain after surgery (e.g. Percocet, hydromorphone, codeine). These medications can be helpful for some people, but they can also be dangerous, particularly when used for a long time. Many patients don't like the way opioids make them feel and would prefer alternative pain management strategies. Some people become addicted to opioids, have a difficult time reducing the dose of opioids, or have lasting health problems after using them. People in this study will be randomized to either have usual care or a new pathway designed to improve pain control and decrease opioid use after knee replacements. This study will have an intervention coordinator who will assess patients before surgery and who will follow up with patients regularly after surgery to make sure their pain is controlled and to avoid long-term opioid use. This study will use education, physiotherapy, psychological therapy, ice/cold, and non-opioid pain medications. As pain medications may work differently in different patients, the coordinator will check on each patient to look for pain control and assist to reduce the amount of opioids used after surgery. This study will help people have safer and more effective pain management after surgery which may lead to better recovery, higher satisfaction, and a lower risk of being harmed by opioids after surgery.
interventions: Multicomponent opioid reduction and pain management pathway
title: Opioid Reduction and Enhanced Recovery in Orthopaedic Surgery (OREOS)-Knee

brief_summary:
Preterm infants born prematurely are more likely to have low zinc levels because they have less time to build up zinc before birth. They also have smaller zinc stores after birth and may need more zinc to support their rapid growth.

This study will examine how growth is affected in premature babies receiving either the current dose or a higher dose of zinc supplementation. The zinc supplement will be given daily, starting according to the unit's standard feeding guidelines, and will be stopped based on usual standard-of-care practices.

Possible risks of zinc supplementation include gastrointestinal intolerance (such as vomiting, diarrhea, or stomach discomfort) and anemia.

Possible benefits include improved growth, a stronger immune system, a shorter hospital stay, and lower healthcare costs.
title: Impact of Higher Zinc Supplementation on Neonatal Weight Velocity

brief_summary: This clinical study evaluates the use of free circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) analysis from peripheral blood, known as liquid biopsy. The objective is to detect minimal residual disease (MRD) early and to predict disease relapse or progression in patients with colorectal cancer (stages II-IV). By monitoring specific KRAS gene mutations (G12 and G13) using the ddPCR method, the study aims to improve risk stratification and treatment response monitoring following primary therapy.
primary_outcomes: ctDNA Detection Rate and Correlation with Minimal Residual Disease (MRD)
title: MRD Monitoring in Colorectal Cancer Using ctDNA

brief_summary: This study aims to compare the therapeutic effects of three different treatment strategies for patients with femoroacetabular impingement. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of three groups: surgery combined with pre-rehabilitation, direct surgery without pre-rehabilitation, or rehabilitation alone. Researchers will follow-up participants and evaluate pain, joint function and other outcomes to find out which treatment works better.
title: Comparison of Surgery With Prehabilitation, Direct Surgery and Rehabilitation for Patients With Femoroacetabular Impingement

brief_summary:
This is a Phase 1 clinical trial to evaluate the safety and tolerability of a new cell therapy called NCR201. The study will enroll adults with moderate-to-advanced primary Parkinson's disease who have previously undergone deep brain stimulation (DBS) surgery.

NCR201 is an investigational cell therapy derived from hypoimmune human induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs). Participants will receive a one-time surgical injection of NCR201 directly into a specific brain region (the putamen) on both sides. The study will use a standard "3+3" design to test two different doses: a low-dose group (4 million cells per side) and a high-dose group (8 million cells per side).

The primary goal of this study is to check for any severe, dose-limiting side effects within the first 8 weeks after surgery, and to determine the maximum tolerated dose or the recommended dose for future Phase 2 studies. Researchers will also look for any initial signs of clinical benefit. Participants will be closely monitored through regular safety and symptom assessments for up to 96 weeks, with an optional long-term safety follow-up lasting an additional 3 to 5 years.
title: A Phase 1 Study of NCR201 in Parkinson's Disease Patients With Prior DBS

brief_summary:
The goal of this Phase II/III study is to investigate the safty and efficacy of 102D-6 in adolescents and adults with influenza.

The main aim to answer:

1. Phase II study is to evaluate the efficacy of 102D-6 in the treatment of adult influenza subjects and determine the optimal therapeutic dose by analyzing the time of virus titer turning to negative. The results will be used to design the Phase III study.
2. Phase III study is to evaluate the efficacy of 102D-6 by analyzing the duration of remission of all influenza symptoms in adolescents and adults subjects with influenza.

Participants will be taken 102D-6/Placebo once, and be observed by 15 days.
primary_outcomes: Phase II:Viral RNA negative conversion time Phase III:time to alleviation of influenza symptoms
title: Evaluation of the Efficacy and Safety of 102D-6 in the Treatment of Acute Uncomplicated Influenza

brief_summary:
The goal of this randomized controlled trial is to evaluate the effectiveness of a 5-week multidimensional intervention in improving ethical decision-making competence among nursing student interns. The intervention is designed to address multiple factors influencing ethical decision-making during clinical training. The study will also examine whether the effects of the intervention are maintained at 1-month and 3-month follow-ups after the intervention ends.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

1. Does the 5-week multidimensional intervention improve ethical decision-making competence among nursing student interns compared with usual clinical internship training?
2. Are the effects of the intervention maintained at 1-month and 3-month follow-ups after the intervention ends?

Researchers will compare nursing student interns who receive the 5-week multidimensional intervention with those who receive usual clinical internship training to evaluate the intervention's effectiveness.

Participants will:

1. Complete questionnaires assessing all study outcome measures at baseline, at the end of the 5-week intervention, and at 1-month and 3-month follow-ups after the intervention ends.
2. Participate in the educational activities provided to their assigned study group.
3. Complete follow-up assessments as scheduled.
conditions: Ethical Decision-Making Competence in Nursing Student Interns
title: A Multidimensional Intervention to Improve Ethical Decision-Making Competence Among Nursing Student Interns: A Randomized Controlled Trial

brief_summary: The primary purpose of this study is to evaluate the effects of combining custom 3D-printed medial arch-supported insoles with short foot exercises on foot posture, balance, and gait parameters in individuals with pes planus (flat feet). Furthermore, the study will investigate the impact of this combined intervention on secondary outcomes, including pain levels, health-related quality of life, and functional exercise capacity measured by the 6-Minute Walk Test.
interventions: Custom 3D Printed Insoles and Short Foot Exercises
primary_outcomes: Spatiotemporal Gait and Plantar Pressure Parameters
title: Effects of Custom 3D Printed Insoles and Short Foot Exercises in Pes Planus

brief_summary:
The aim of this study is to investigate the relationship of Q-angle, lower extremity segment lengths, and quadriceps muscle activation with dynamic knee alignment during a single-leg squat in active soccer players.

Study hypotheses:

H1: There is a significant relationship between Q-angle and dynamic knee alignment during a single-leg squat in active soccer players.

H2: There is a significant relationship between femur length and dynamic knee alignment during a single-leg squat in active soccer players.

H3: There is a significant relationship between tibia length and dynamic knee alignment during a single-leg squat in active soccer players.

H4: There is a significant relationship between the ratio of lower extremity segment lengths and dynamic knee alignment during a single-leg squat in active soccer players.

H5: There is a significant relationship between the level of quadriceps muscle activation and dynamic knee alignment during a single-leg squat in active soccer players.

H6: When Q-angle, lower extremity segment lengths, and quadriceps muscle activation are evaluated together, they are significantly associated with dynamic knee alignment during a single-leg squat in active soccer players.
title: Q-Angle, Segment Length, Quadriceps, and Knee Alignment in Soccer Players

brief_summary:
Moyamoya disease is a relatively rare chronic cerebrovascular disease, and its exact cause is currently unknown. This disease is characterized by the gradual narrowing or even blockage of important blood vessels in the brain (the terminal portion of the internal carotid artery), while simultaneously forming an abnormal network of small blood vessels at the base of the brain. In cerebral angiography, these abnormal vessels appear as a cloud of "smoke," hence the name "Moyamoya disease." Patients with Moyamoya disease often present with cerebral hemorrhage or cerebral infarction as the initial manifestation, which can seriously affect their quality of life and even endanger their lives.

In recent years, with the development of imaging examinations (such as CT, MRI, and cerebral angiography), more and more patients are being diagnosed in a timely manner. However, because the cause is still unclear, there is currently no specific drug to cure the disease. Clinically, medication is mainly used to prevent thrombosis and stabilize blood vessels, such as commonly used...

Aspirin and atorvastatin are used to reduce the risk of cerebral infarction or cerebral hemorrhage and slow the progression of the disease.

Currently, the main treatment for Moyamoya disease remains surgery (revascularization surgery), which aims to reduce seizures by improving blood supply to the brain. However, surgery has certain limitations, such as being technically challenging, carrying high risks, and potentially leading to postoperative complications, and it still cannot completely stop disease progression.

In Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) theory, Moyamoya disease is often associated with "phlegm and dampness" and "blood stasis." Simply put, "phlegm and dampness" and "poor blood circulation" in the body affect the normal blood supply and function of the brain, leading to blood vessel blockage or rupture and bleeding. Therefore, TCM treatment typically focuses on \*\*"promoting blood circulation and removing blood stasis, clearing heat and cooling blood, and unblocking the meridians and opening the orifices"\*\*.

"Liangxue Tongyu Fang" is a traditional Chinese medicine formula primarily used to improve hemorrhagic cerebrovascular diseases. Through the combined effects of various Chinese herbs, this formula may help improve blood circulation, reduce vascular damage, and promote brain function recovery.

Currently, this formula has been used in some hemorrhagic encephalopathy cases and has shown certain therapeutic effects. This study will use clinical research methods to observe the safety (whether it will produce significant adverse reactions) and effectiveness (whether it helps improve the condition or reduce recurrence) of "Liangxue Tongyu Fang" in patients with hemorrhagic moyamoya disease, in order to provide more new options and evidence for the treatment of moyamoya disease.
lead_sponsor: The First Affiliated Hospital with Nanjing Medical University
primary_outcomes: Percentage of Participants With an Increase of at Least 1 Point in Cerebral Perfusion Staging Score
title: Clinical Safety and Efficacy Evaluation of the Blood-cooling and Stasis-removing Formula as an Adjunct to Atorvastatin in the Treatment of Hemorrhagic Moyamoya Disease.

brief_summary:
The SELDISC trial will investigate whether a selective nerve root block can reduce the need for surgery in adults with a herniated disc in the lower back. A herniated disc can irritate a nerve and cause pain that travels down the leg. A nerve root block delivers a local anaesthetic and a corticosteroid near the affected nerve to relieve pain and inflammation.

The study will include 262 adults aged 18-66 years who have persistent leg symptoms despite non-surgical treatment and have been assessed by a spine surgeon as eligible for surgery.

Participants will be randomly assigned to receive either a selective nerve root block or a sham procedure that mimics the treatment without delivering the active medication near the nerve. Each participant will have an equal chance of receiving either procedure. Participants and the study staff assessing their outcomes will not know which procedure was given. The radiologist performing the procedure will know the allocation.

The main question is whether fewer participants in the nerve root block group undergo surgery within 12 months after randomisation. The study will also compare pain, disability, quality of life, time to surgery, medication use, sick leave, healthcare use and adverse events between the groups.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of participants undergoing lumbar disc surgery
title: Selective Nerve Root Block Versus Sham to Reduce Surgery for Lumbar Disc Herniation

brief_summary:
This randomized controlled study aims to evaluate the effects of an eight-week, group-based positive psychology program on hope, gratitude, and mental well-being among adults aged 65 years and older living in nursing homes in Gaziantep, Türkiye. Approximately 60 participants will be assigned to an intervention group or a control group, with 30 participants planned for each group.

The intervention group will receive eight weekly positive psychology sessions, each lasting 40-45 minutes, based on the PERMA model and adapted to older adults. The program will address positive emotions, engagement, relationships, meaning in life, accomplishment, hope, gratitude, and psychological well-being. The control group will receive no intervention during the study period and will be provided with an educational guide about the program after study completion.

Hope, gratitude, and mental well-being will be assessed using the Herth Hope Scale, Gratitude Scale, and Warwick-Edinburgh Mental Well-Being Scale, respectively. Assessments will be conducted before the intervention, immediately after the eight-week program, and at a two-month follow-up. The study aims to determine whether the positive psychology program improves these outcomes among older adults living in nursing homes.
title: Effects of Positive Psychology on Hope, Gratitude, and Well-Being

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if a touchscreen-based virtual reality (VR) training program that simulates everyday life tasks works to improve daily living skills and thinking abilities in adults aged 50 and older, including those at risk of dementia (individuals with Subjective Cognitive Decline or Mild Cognitive Impairment). It will also explore what personal factors influence the training results. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does the daily life VR training program improve participants' ability to perform complex everyday activities and adapt flexibly to daily life challenges?
* Does the training improve overall thinking skills (such as memory, attention, and problem-solving), brain activity, and mood (depression and anxiety)? Researchers will compare the daily-life VR training program (IADL-VR) to a non-situational game VR program (Game-VR) and a traditional in-person tabletop cognitive training program (Cog-Entity) to see if realistic daily-life VR simulation works better to enhance everyday functioning and brain health.

Participants will:

* Be randomly assigned to one of the three training groups (daily-life VR tasks, digital brain-training mini-games, or traditional tabletop board games).
* Attend a 2-hour group session once a week for 12 weeks, which includes 1 hour of assigned cognitive training and 1 hour of physical fitness exercise.
* Complete assessments of their daily living skills, thinking abilities, mood, and brain activity (using functional magnetic resonance imaging, or fMRI) within 2 weeks before and after the 12-week program.
primary_outcomes: The Brief University of California San Diego Performance-Based Skills Assessment-Traditional Chinese Version (UPSA-B)
title: The Efficacy of an IADL-based Non-immersive Virtual Reality Training Program to Enhance ADL Performance and Cognitive Function for Persons at Risk of Dementia

brief_summary: Premature Infant Oral Motor Intervention (PIOMI) has been found to improve short-term clinical outcomes in preterm infants and contribute to their feeding skills. In preterm infants, PIOMI can improve weight and facilitate early oral feeding. Furthermore, PIOMI can shorten the length of hospital stay and the separation time between the infant and caregiver in preterm infants. The primary aim of this project is to evaluate the effect of PIOMI in mother-infant interaction (applied with the infant in the mother's arms and accompanied by the mother's voice) on feeding readiness, suckling success, mothers' breastfeeding attitudes and infants' feeding maturity in preterm newborns. The secondary objective is to investigate whether PIOMI applied in mother-infant interaction affects mothers' positive and negative emotional states.
interventions: The PIOMI initiative in maternal interaction
primary_outcomes: Overlapped Inspirium After Swallow Events: Overlapped Inspirium After Swallow Percentage & Average Overlapped Inspirium After Swallow Duration
title: Nutritional Maturity in Preterm Newborns (Premature Infant Oral Motor Intervention, PIOMI)

brief_summary:
The purpose of this study is to investigate the efficacy and safety of HRS-6209 in combination with letrozole compared with dalpciclib or palbociclib in combination with aromatase inhibitor in patients with advanced or metastatic breast cancer who have not received prior systemic treatment for advanced or metastatic disease.

Approximately half of the participants will receive HRS-6209 plus letrozole while the other half of participants will receive dalpciclib or palbociclib in combination with aromatase inhibitor.

The study team will monitor how each participant is doing with the study treatment during regular visits at the study clinic.
primary_outcomes: Progression-Free Survival (PFS) Determined by Blinded Independent Central Review (BICR)
title: A Phase III Clinical Study of HRS-6209 Plus Letrozole as First-line Therapy in Patients With Advanced or Metastatic Breast Cancer

brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to compare the immunogenicity and safety of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccination between lung transplant recipients and immunocompetent adults and to provide evidence to guide RSV vaccination in lung transplant recipients.
title: Immunogenicity and Safety of Respiratory Syncytial Virus Vaccine in Lung Transplant Recipients

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn which type of exercise before surgery best reduces complications after colorectal surgery in adults with colorectal cancer or precancerous lesions. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does resistance (strength) training, aerobic (endurance) training, or a combination of both before surgery lower the rate and severity of complications in the first 30 days after surgery, compared with no exercise program?
* Which factors influence how well patients follow a prehabilitation program, and does following the program affect surgical outcomes?

Researchers will compare three exercise groups with a control group that receives standard care without an exercise program.

Participants will:

* Be randomly assigned to one of four groups: resistance training, aerobic training, combined training, or no exercise program (control)
* Do the assigned home exercise program for 4 to 6 weeks before surgery, with weekly physiotherapy check-ups in person or by phone
* Receive nutritional counseling, breathing exercises, and psychological support if needed, regardless of group
* Keep a daily exercise diary and record their pulse daily
* Undergo physical fitness tests (walking test, sit-to-stand test, handgrip strength) and quality-of-life questionnaires before surgery and 8 weeks after surgery
title: Resistance vs Aerobic Prehabilitation Before Colorectal Cancer Surgery

brief_summary:
Hospitalization for RSV lower respiratory tract infections (LRTI) still occurs, including in infants having received nirsevimab/clesrovimab or born to mothers vaccinated with Abrysvo.

We hypothesize that pediatric patients hospitalized for RSV LRTIs occurring in the era of large use of prophylaxis, could be, at least in part, explained by virological factors (emergence/selection of variants with decreased susceptibility to prophylaxis) and/or immunological factors (inherited immune deficiency, presence of auto-antibodies neutralizing anti-viral cytokines such as type I interferons, impaired mucosal responses or mucosal pharmacokinetics issues inducing low levels of local concentrations of nirsevimab/clesrovimab).
conditions: Children <24 Months Hospitalized for RSV-related Lower Respiratory Tract Infection
interventions: Prior exposure to prophylactic treatment with Abrysvo or nirsevimab/clesrovimab
primary_outcomes: RSV variants with reduced sensitivity to prophylaxis
title: Severe Pediatric Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infections Occurring in the Era of Antiviral Prophylaxis

brief_summary: This study will compare live video-based and prerecorded video-based Pilates programs in 38 adults aged 18-65 years with multiple sclerosis. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of two groups. The live-session group will exercise with a physiotherapist twice a week for eight weeks, with sessions lasting 45-60 minutes. The prerecorded-video group will follow an exercise program matched in intensity and progressed every two weeks, using an exercise tracking form. Trunk muscle performance, balance, thinking and memory, and quality of life will be assessed before and after the program. The study aims to determine whether live supervision provides additional benefits compared with prerecorded exercise videos.
title: The Effects of Synchronous and Asynchronous Pilates Training Based on Telerehabilitation on Core Stabilization, Balance, Cognitive Functions, and Quality of Life in Individuals With Multiple Sclerosis: A Single-Blind Randomized Controlled Trial

brief_summary:
Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) is increasingly used as rescue support in patients with refractory respiratory and/or circulatory failure. ECMO cannula site infection (ECMO-CSI) complicates approximately 10% of ECMO runs and is associated with septic shock, prolonged intensive care unit (ICU) stay and increased mortality. To date, there is neither a standardized definition nor consensus diagnostic criteria for ECMO-CSI, and the optimal microbiological sampling strategy, as well as the diagnostic accuracy of the available methods, remains undetermined.

This single-center, prospective, non-interventional study aims to compare the diagnostic accuracy of three microbiological sampling methods (superficial swab of the cannula insertion site, needle aspiration along the cannula tract, and cannula tip culture) for the diagnosis of ECMO-CSI in adult patients receiving veno-venous or veno-arterial ECMO.

A superficial swab and a needle aspirate will be obtained at each cannulation site on the day ECMO-CSI is clinically suspected and on the day of decannulation. In addition, the tip of each cannula will be cultured at decannulation. The results of these index tests will be compared with a reference diagnosis of ECMO-CSI established by an adjudication committee of expert clinicians blinded to the index test results.

A total of 500 patients will be enrolled in order to obtain at least 50 patients with adjudicated ECMO-CSI.
primary_outcomes: Diagnostic performance of each sampling strategy (superficial swab, needle aspiration, cannula tip culture) for the diagnosis of ECMO cannula infection
title: Diagnosis of ECMO Cannula Infection: Prospective Comparison of Sampling Methods
[Trial of device that is not approved or cleared by the U.S. FDA]

brief_summary: The aim of this study is to demonstrate the clinical efficacy of the Test Toothpaste containing Calcium Sodium Phosphosilicate (CSPS) in reducing Dentin Hypersensitivity (DH) to an evaporative (air) stimulus, compared to a sodium fluoride Reference Toothpaste, after 8 Weeks of twice daily use.
primary_outcomes: Change from Baseline in Schiff Sensitivity Score at Week 8
title: A Study to Assess the Efficacy of a Calcium Sodium Phosphosilicate Toothpaste for the Relief of Dentine Hypersensitivity

brief_summary:
This non-inferiority trial will compare conventional long-course accelerated fractionation radiation therapy (AF-RT) with volumetric adaptive stereotactic body radiation therapy (SBRT) in patients with early-stage (cT1-2N0M0) glottic squamous cell carcinoma. Participants will be randomized in a 1:2 ratio to receive either AF-RT (Arm A) or adaptive SBRT (Arm B).

The primary objective is to determine whether adaptive SBRT provides non-inferior local control compared with AF-RT in patients with early-stage glottic squamous cell carcinoma. Secondary analyses will evaluate treatment-related toxicity and other clinical outcomes.

The study hypothesizes that adaptive SBRT will achieve local control rates that are non-inferior to those of AF-RT while offering a substantially shorter treatment course. Imaging biomarkers, transcriptome/methylome profiles, plasma biomarkers, and cfDNA will be analyzed to identify novel biomarkers that predict oncologic outcomes and treatment-related toxicity.
interventions: Long course accelerated fractionation radiation therapy
title: Volumetric Adaptive SBRT Versus Conventional Accelerated Radiation Therapy for Early-Stage Glottic Cancer

brief_summary:
The goal of this exploratory clinical trial is to characterize and compare skin clinical signs, skin physiology and subjective well-being before and after CO₂ fractional laser or Thermage treatment. It will also explore correlations between skin parameters and investigate the optimal timing for starting skincare products after the procedure. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* How do skin clinical signs, physiological indicators and subjective well-being change pre- and post-procedure for CO₂ fractional laser and Thermage?
* Are there correlations between different skin parameters before and after the aesthetic procedure?
* When is the optimal time to begin using skincare products after treatment?

Researchers will compare CO₂ fractional laser versus Thermage. Clinical assessors remain blinded to treatment group assignment; participants are unblinded due to visible procedural effects.

Participants will:

* Use only neutral skincare products (cream + sunscreen) during a 2-week wash-out period
* Receive one session of either CO₂ fractional laser or Thermage treatment
* Complete a 10-day self-recovery period, then attend follow-up assessments for up to 12 weeks
* Maintain neutral skincare products (cream + sunscreen) for the full 12-week post-treatment phase
* Attend clinic visits for skin clinical and physiological evaluations
conditions: Skin Physiology After Fractional CO₂ Laser Treatment
primary_outcomes: Clinical Grading by Dermatologist for efficacy
title: Pre- and Post-procedure Skin Knowledge Study

brief_summary: This study is a single-arm, prospective, multi-center, Phase IIIb clinical trial aimed at evaluating the efficacy and safety of the maximum labeled dose of luspatercept in individuals diagnosed with lower-risk myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS). The trial anticipates the enrollment of 75 participants with lower-risk MDS, all of whom will undergo treatment with luspatercept.
lead_sponsor: Institute of Hematology & Blood Diseases Hospital, China
primary_outcomes: Proportion of patients achieving red blood cell transfusion independence (RBC-TI) for at least 8 weeks
title: Efficacy and Safety of Maximum Labeled Dose Luspatercept in Lower-Risk Myelodysplastic Syndromes

brief_summary:
This study was planned to determine the effect of using a birthing stool during labor on birth comfort, perceived support and control during labor in primiparous pregnant women.

H1: Primiparous pregnant women who use a drape during labor have higher birth comfort compared to those who do not.

H2: Primiparous pregnant women who use a drape during labor have higher levels of birth control and support compared to those who do not.

H3: Primiparous pregnant women who use a drape during labor have shorter labor durations compared to those who do not.
primary_outcomes: Duration of the active phase of labor (minutes)
title: Effect of Birthing Stool Use During Labor on Birth Comfort, Perceived Support and Control

brief_summary: Para-aortic lymphadenectomy plays an important role in the surgical treatment of major gynecological malignancies (ovarian, endometrial, and cervical cancer). Identifying bilateral ureters is a crucial step, and dissecting the upper left ureter is particularly challenging with no standardized method. This study introduces an anatomical technique called the "One-Finger Technique" for this purpose. This prospective, single-arm exploratory study aims to evaluate the feasibility and safety of the "One-Finger Technique" during open para-aortic lymphadenectomy.

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate the effect of planned group interaction on ostomy adaptation, quality of life, and stoma care self-efficacy in adult individuals (aged 18 and older) living with a stoma.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

Does planned group interaction improve ostomy adaptation levels in individuals with a stoma? Does planned group interaction positively affect the quality of life in individuals with a stoma? Does planned group interaction positively affect stoma care self-efficacy in individuals with a stoma? Researchers will compare a control group receiving routine care and education to an experimental group receiving the intervention to see if planned group interactions lead to better adaptation, higher quality of life, and increased self-efficacy.

Participants will:

Attend weekly planned group interaction and education sessions lasting 60-90 minutes for a total of 5 weeks (Experimental group only).

Engage in guided group discussions, under the supervision of faculty members and nurses, to share experiences and learn about physical, psychosocial, and sexual issues, as well as complications related to living with a stoma (Experimental group only).

Continue to receive their routine stoma care and standard education without attending group sessions (Control group).

Complete a set of questionnaires, including a Descriptive Characteristics Form, Ostomy Adjustment Inventory, Stoma Quality of Life Scale, and Stoma Self-Efficacy Scale, at the beginning of the study (pre-test) and at the end of the 5-week period (post-test).
primary_outcomes: Change in Stoma Quality of Life Score

title: The Effect of Planned Group Interaction on Ostomy Adaptation, Quality of Life, and Stoma Care Self-Efficacy Levels in Individuals With an Ostomy

brief_summary:
The goal of this study is to measure how well commonly used antibiotics reach the tissue in the head and neck region in adults with a postoperative neck infection or undergoing reconstructive nasal surgery with an inferior turbinate flap. The study also describes markers of ischemia and inflammation in the newly created flap during the first days after surgery.

The main question it aims to answer is: For how long do the free concentrations of cefuroxime, cloxacillin, dicloxacillin, and amoxicillin/clavulanic acid stay above the minimal inhibitory concentration (T\>MIC) in infected tissue, non-infected tissue, the flap, and plasma?

Participants will receive the antibiotics on a fixed, protocol-defined schedule for about two days. Small microdialysis catheters will be placed in the tissue to collect fluid continuously, and serial blood samples will be drawn. Participation ends when the last sample is collected and the catheters are removed.
primary_outcomes: Time Above the Minimal Inhibitory Concentration (T>MIC) in Tissue and Plasma

These fractures may be treated using an isolated anterior approach with posterior column screw fixation or through sequential anterior and posterior column fixation. The relative benefits and risks of these two strategies remain uncertain.

This prospective randomized controlled trial will compare isolated fixation through the modified Stoppa approach with posterior column screws versus sequential anterior and posterior column fixation in participants with double-column acetabular fractures. Thirty participants will be randomly allocated to the two treatment groups. The study will compare radiological and functional outcomes, implant failure, recurrent diastasis, operative characteristics, complications, wound infection, and the need for additional surgery.

brief_summary:
The purpose of this prospective observational cohort study is to determine whether the amount of fat inside the donor muscles before surgery, measured with a magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) technique called Dixon fat fraction (FF), can predict how much ankle dorsiflexion strength patients with Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease (CMT) recover after tibialis posterior tendon transfer surgery.

CMT is an inherited nerve disease that weakens the feet and legs, causing foot drop and high-arched, inwardly turned feet. A common operation transfers the tibialis posterior tendon to the top of the foot to restore foot lifting; however, the transplanted muscle itself may be weakened by fatty degeneration, and surgeons currently have no objective way to know in advance how well the transferred muscle will work.

We hypothesize that a lower preoperative fat fraction of the tibialis posterior (donor) muscle is associated with greater recovery of dorsiflexion strength after surgery.

A total of 100 adults (18-55 years) with genetically confirmed CMT types 1A, 1X or 2A who are scheduled for individualized foot surgery that includes tibialis posterior tendon transfer will be enrolled at 4 foot-and-ankle centers in China.

Within 1 month before surgery, participants will undergo a lower-leg MRI with a Dixon sequence to measure the fat fraction of 11 calf muscles. Participants will then be followed for 5 years (3 and 6 months, and 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 years after surgery).

At every visit, ankle dorsiflexion strength will be measured with a hand-held dynamometer and normalized to body weight (newtons per kilogram); walking ability (1-minute walk distance, 10-meter walking speed), ankle range of motion, clinical severity scales (CMTES, Walk-12, FADI, SF-12) and CMT-related symptoms (pain, fatigue, cramps, balance and falls, sensory loss, hand function, brace use, calluses, mood) will also be assessed. Surgical details of every additional procedure will be recorded.

The primary analysis will correlate preoperative tibialis posterior fat fraction with the change in dorsiflexion strength at each time point (principal endpoint: 12 months), and will test whether fat fraction independently predicts strength recovery in a multivariable regression model.

If confirmed, preoperative muscle fat fraction could become an objective, readily available imaging marker to help surgeons select patients, choose between tendon transfer alternatives, and counsel patients about expected outcomes.
interventions: Individualized adjunct procedures for cavovarus deformity correction
primary_outcomes: Change From Baseline in Maximum Isometric Ankle Dorsiflexion Strength at Each Postoperative Time Point
title: Muscle MRI Fat Fraction Before Surgery to Predict Strength Recovery After Foot-Drop Surgery in Charcot-Marie-Tooth Disease

brief_summary: This study is a prospective single-arm clinical trial targeting patients with stage IB-IIIA non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) who have received neoadjuvant immunotherapy. The primary objective is to evaluate whether a personalized follow-up and adjuvant treatment strategy-based on the combination of ctDNA-based minimal residual disease (MRD) testing and pathological response-can effectively improve the 2-year postoperative recurrence-free survival (RFS). The study will enroll 100 patients scheduled for radical surgery who have undergone neoadjuvant immunotherapy (in combination with platinum-based chemotherapy). Patients will receive individualized follow-up and adjuvant therapy based on dynamic changes in ctDNA at various preoperative and postoperative timepoints, as well as pathological response. Adjuvant therapy will be recommended if patients do not achieve pathological complete response (pCR) after surgery, or if ctDNA testing is positive after neoadjuvant therapy or post-surgery. Only patients who achieve pCR and have negative ctDNA at both specified timepoints will forgo adjuvant therapy; these patients will undergo blood sampling at each routine follow-up, with adjuvant therapy initiated upon ctDNA seroconversion to positive. The primary endpoint is 2-year RFS after surgery; secondary endpoints include overall survival (OS) and the diagnostic rate of recurrence/metastasis based on ctDNA-MRD testing. This project aims to explore the refinement of adaptive treatment strategies in the neoadjuvant immunotherapy lung cancer population, with the ultimate goal of improving overall therapeutic efficacy and establishing a standardized, integrated postoperative management system suitable for lung cancer patients.
interventions: Adaptive therapy of de-escalation and escalation based on MRD testing and pathological response
title: MRD-Guided Postoperative Surveillance and Adaptive Treatment for Resectable Lung Cancer

brief_summary:
This pilot controlled study aims to evaluate the clinical and instrumental effects and feasibility of transcutaneous cervical spinal cord stimulation (tSCS) combined with conventional rehabilitation in adults with spinal cord injury (SCI).

A total of 20 participants will be enrolled and assigned to two parallel groups. The experimental group will receive conventional rehabilitation combined with transcutaneous cervical spinal cord stimulation using the ExaStim® system, while the control group will receive conventional rehabilitation alone. In the experimental group, stimulation will be delivered twice weekly for 4 weeks, for a total of 8 sessions.

The study will primarily explore the immediate effects of a single stimulation session on motor control and muscle tone. It will also assess changes in motor function, muscle tone, and clinical, robotic, and electrophysiological measures over the 4-week intervention period, as well as feasibility, tolerability, and adverse events. Comparisons between the experimental and control groups will be exploratory, consistent with the pilot nature of the study.
title: Transcutaneous Spinal Cord Stimulation for Neurorehabilitation After Spinal Cord Injury

brief_summary:
This randomized controlled trial aims to investigate whether a brief clinical hypnosis intervention can reduce dissociative symptoms more effectively than guided imagery in adults receiving psychiatric care.

Dissociative symptoms may include feelings of detachment from oneself or the surrounding environment, difficulties with memory, changes in the sense of identity, and a reduced sense of control over one's experiences. These symptoms can interfere with everyday functioning and occur across different mental health conditions.

The study will enroll approximately 160 adults with clinically significant dissociative symptoms. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of two groups: clinical hypnosis or non-hypnotic guided imagery. Both interventions will consist of four individual, in-person sessions lasting approximately 50 minutes each, delivered over 4-6 weeks alongside usual psychiatric care.

The clinical hypnosis intervention is designed to help participants recognize changes in their mental and bodily experiences, maintain awareness during these changes, and practice intentionally regulating them. The guided imagery intervention focuses on relaxation, sensory awareness, grounding, and emotional stabilization without using hypnosis-specific techniques.

The main outcome will be the severity of dissociative symptoms, measured using the Dissociative Experiences Scale-II (DES-II) approximately one week after the final session. Additional assessments will examine quality of life, psychological symptoms, and the safety and tolerability of both interventions. Follow-up evaluations at 3 and 6 months will assess whether any changes in dissociative symptoms are maintained.

The study will also explore whether participants' sense of control over their experiences may help explain treatment-related changes in dissociative symptoms.
primary_outcomes: Dissociative Symptom Severity (DES-II Total Score) Copia
title: Clinical Hypnosis Versus Guided Imagery for Dissociative Symptoms in Adults

brief_summary: Total anesthesia is the most commonly used anesthesia method in clinical surgery, which can reduce hospital stay and improve patient comfort on the basis of ensuring patient surgery safety. However, for patients with total anaesthetic tracheotomy, the incidence of throat complications such as throat pain, wheezing, and coughing after tracheotomy removal remains high. According to literature reports, the incidence of throat pain can reach 40% after total anaesthetic tracheotomy removal, the incidence of wheezing is 24%, and the related throat symptoms can persist until 24 hours or even longer after surgery. This phenomenon is particularly notable in patients with thoracic surgery.The high incidence of laryngeal pain after thoracic surgery is the result of the combination of mechanical stimulation of the bronchial / bilateral bronchial catheter, air sac pressure, surgery time and position, individual susceptibility factors of the patient, and technical details of intubation/entubation. Although such laryngeal complications are milder compared to other anesthetic complications, they can reduce the patient's post-operative hospitalization comfort and satisfaction, and even prolong the hospitalization time, affecting clinical treatment effectiveness and patient admission experience.This study aims to explore the effect of polycamomile lidocaine gel as a bronchial catheter lubricant on postoperative laryngeal complications in patients undergoing thoracic surgery. It aims to provide new ideas and clinical basis for optimizing clinical drug administration protocols and reducing the incidence of postoperative laryngeal complications for patients undergoing thoracic surgery with total anaesthetic bronchial intubation.

primary_outcomes: Baseline-corrected delta in CPPS (dB) for the sustained vowel /ɑ/ stable segment at 6 hours post-extubation (ΔCPPS₆ₕ = CPPS₆ₕ - CPPSₚᵣₑ)
title: The Effect of Compound Chamomile and Lidocaine Hydronchloride Gel as an Endotracheal Tube Lubricant on Postoperative Pharyngeal and Laryngeal Complications in Thoracic Surgery Patients

brief_summary: This study evaluates the impact of preventive ovarian reserve screening and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled counseling on fertility awareness and reproductive anxiety among women in Hong Kong. Hong Kong faces low birth rates, and reproductive anxiety regarding the biological clock remains a key barrier to family planning. Participants aged 25 to 38 years will be allocated to receive either anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH) blood testing combined with counseling or standard health education materials. The study compares an interactive AI conversational agent ("Shelby") with traditional written reports to evaluate whether AI communication improves comprehension of medical results, reduces anxiety, and enhances fertility intentions. Findings aim to inform future public health screening policies.
