brief_summary:
Background: Ankylosing spondylitis (AS) is a chronic, progressive inflammatory disease mainly affecting the spine and sacroiliac joints, causing pain, stiffness, structural damage, and functional disability. NSAIDs remain first-line therapy, while biologics and JAK inhibitors have expanded treatment options. However, many patients have inadequate responses or residual symptoms, and long-term combination with NSAIDs is common despite uncertain incremental benefit. Ivarmacitinib is a highly selective oral JAK1 inhibitor that has shown efficacy in active AS. Whether concomitant celecoxib adds benefit to ivarmacitinib monotherapy remains unknown.

Objectives: To compare the efficacy and safety of ivarmacitinib plus celecoxib versus ivarmacitinib monotherapy in patients with active AS. The primary objective is to compare the proportion achieving an ASAS20 response at week 24.

Methods: This prospective, single-center, randomized, open-label, parallel-group, active-controlled superiority trial will enroll 138 patients with active AS (BASDAI ≥4 and total back pain VAS ≥4) who had inadequate response to at least two NSAIDs or intolerance/contraindication to NSAIDs. Participants will be randomized 1:1 to ivarmacitinib 4 mg once daily plus celecoxib 200 mg twice daily or ivarmacitinib 4 mg once daily for 48 weeks, with as-needed rescue analgesia permitted. The study is open-label, but endpoint assessors and the statistician will be blinded. Key exclusion criteria include prior JAK inhibitor use, major cardiovascular events, active peptic ulcer or bleeding, moderate-to-severe renal insufficiency, pregnancy, significant laboratory abnormalities, and malignancy within 5 years.

Outcomes: The primary endpoint is the proportion achieving ASAS20 at week 24. Secondary endpoints include ASAS20 at weeks 12 and 48; ASAS40 and ASAS5/6; changes in BASDAI, ASDAS-CRP, CRP, ESR, BASMI, BASFI, pain VAS, ASQoL, MASES, GUESS, and SPARCC MRI score; rescue analgesic use; and adverse event incidence, type, severity, and relatedness, with attention to gastrointestinal, cardiovascular, renal, and infectious risks.

Sample Size: Assuming a week-24 ASAS20 rate of 66.7% in the combination group, a 25-percentage-point superiority margin, two-sided α = 0.05, 80% power, and 15% dropout, 69 patients per group are required (total 138).

Statistical Analysis: The full analysis set includes all randomized patients receiving at least one dose, analyzed as randomized. The primary analysis will compare week-24 ASAS20 proportions using a normal-approximation Z-test with 95% CI and p-value; significance is p ≤ 0.025 one-sided. Secondary categorical endpoints will use the Z-test with non-responder imputation; continuous variables will use MMRM or ANCOVA. Safety will be analyzed descriptively in the safety set.

Expected Significance: This trial will provide prospective, head-to-head evidence on whether regular celecoxib adds benefit to ivarmacitinib monotherapy, informing individualized NSAID-JAK inhibitor combination decisions and supporting evidence-based optimization of AS treatment.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of participants achieving an ASAS20 response at week 24.
title: Ivarmacitinib With or Without Celecoxib for Ankylosing Spondylitis

brief_summary: Research objective: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of gematinib combined with lenvatinib in the treatment of advanced or metastatic NSCLC with MET overexpression that has failed standard therapy Experimental design: Prospective, multicenter, single-arm Study population: Patients with locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC who have overexpression of the MET protein (IHC 3+: ≥ 50% of tumor cells show strong positivity; IHC 2+: ≥ 50% of tumor cells show moderate positivity) Sample size: 23 cases (including 6 cases in the safety introduction period) Drug regimen: Gematinib: 300mg, orally, once daily; Lenvatinib: For patients with a body weight of less than 60 kg, 8 mg once daily; for patients with a body weight of 60 kg or more, 12 mg once daily. A 21-day cycle is used until disease progression, occurrence of intolerable adverse reactions, or the subject withdrawing from the study.
title: Gematinib Combined With Lenvatinib for the Treatment of Locally Advanced or Metastatic Non-small Cell Lung Cancer With MET Protein Overexpression: A Prospective, Multicenter, Phase II Clinical Study

brief_summary:
This study will investigate whether adding cognitive tasks to core stabilization exercises improves the ability to perform physical and mental tasks simultaneously in adults with chronic nonspecific low back pain.

A total of 90 participants aged 18-55 years will be randomly assigned to one of two groups. Both groups will complete the same supervised core stabilization exercise program, consisting of 18 sessions over six weeks. In the dual-task group, participants will perform cognitive activities, such as mental arithmetic and memory tasks, while exercising. In the single-task group, participants will perform the same exercises without additional cognitive tasks.

The primary outcome will be motor dual-task cost during the Timed Up and Go test, which measures the change in functional mobility performance when a cognitive task is performed simultaneously. Secondary outcomes will include cognitive dual-task performance, walking speed, balance, pain intensity, disability, and fear of movement.

Assessments will be conducted before treatment, immediately after the intervention, and at the 12-week follow-up.

The study aims to determine whether combining cognitive and physical tasks during core stabilization training provides additional benefits compared with conventional core stabilization exercises alone.
primary_outcomes: Motor Dual-Task Cost During the Timed Up and Go Test
title: Dual-Task Core Stabilization Training in Chronic Nonspecific Low Back Pain

brief_summary:
This clinical trial aims to investigate if oral immunotherapy can help children with peanut allergy tolerate peanut.

Children aged 6 months to 4 years can take part in the trial.

Main question: What percentage of children can tolerate peanut after oral immunotherapy, compared with children who avoid peanut?

Children are assigned to these two groups by chance.

Children receiving oral immunotherapy will:

* Take a small, increasing amount of peanut daily for 1-1.5 years
* Attend clinic or online visits each time the dose is increased
* Record missed doses

All children will:

* Provide blood samples to measure allergy-related markers
* Undergo an oral food challenge with peanut after 1-1.5 years to assess how much they can tolerate

* Participate in an end-of-study telephone interview with an allergy nurse (parent-reported)

brief_summary:

Researchers will analyze these samples for circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA), small fragments of DNA released into the bloodstream by cancer cells, to monitor how the cancer responds to treatment.

The information gained from this study may help improve treatment planning, disease monitoring, and overall outcomes for patients with bladder cancer.

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if electroencephalogram (EEG) biofeedback-guided transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) works to treat swallowing difficulties (dysphagia) in adults after a stroke. It will also learn about the safety of this rehabilitation method and how it helps the brain recover. The main questions it aims to answer are:

1. Does EEG biofeedback-guided taVNS improve the ability to eat and drink by mouth?
2. What medical problems (adverse events) do participants have during the treatment?

Researchers will compare EEG biofeedback-guided taVNS (where gentle electrical stimulation to the outer ear is paired with surface brainwave monitoring during swallowing exercises) to conventional taVNS (where electrical stimulation is given at fixed times) to see which method better improves swallowing function.

Participants will:

1. Receive standardized swallowing rehabilitation training for at least 30 minutes a day, 5 days a week for 2 weeks.
2. Practice swallowing imagery exercises with non-invasive surface EEG biofeedback monitoring while receiving gentle taVNS on the outer ear for 20 minutes a day, 5 days a week for 2 weeks.
3. Complete swallowing tests, questionnaires, and brain evaluations before treatment, after the 2-week treatment, and at Week 4 for follow-up.
lead_sponsor: First Affiliated Hospital of Fujian Medical University
title: EEG Feedback-Based Vagus Nerve Stimulation for Post-Stroke Dysphagia

brief_summary:
This is a Phase 1, single-center, open-label study designed to evaluate the effect of itraconazole on the pharmacokinetics of HRS-4642 in healthy adult participants.

Approximately 18 healthy participants will be enrolled. Each participant will receive HRS-4642 alone by intravenous infusion, followed by HRS-4642 in combination with oral itraconazole. Blood samples will be collected to measure HRS-4642 concentrations and assess whether itraconazole affects how HRS-4642 is processed by the body.

The safety of HRS-4642 administered alone and in combination with itraconazole will also be evaluated throughout the study.

brief_summary: Chronic kidney disease affects approximately 10% of the world population. End-stage renal disease (ESRD) is associated with immune dysregulation, chronic inflammation, and alteration of the gut and urinary microbiota. Kidney transplantation is the reference treatment for ESRD, but required immunosuppressive therapy further aggravates immune dysregulation and is associated with cardiovascular, metabolic and infectious complications. The gut microbiota plays a central role in modulating systemic immunity. In ESRD, microbiota composition is strongly altered. A recent study showed an association between gut dysbiosis and all-cause mortality in over 1,300 kidney transplant recipients. However, the mechanisms underlying deleterious microbiota modifications in transplant recipients remain poorly understood, particularly the respective roles of immunosuppressive treatment and renal function recovery. The MICRO-KT study hypothesizes that the programmed introduction of immunosuppressive therapy followed by partial or complete correction of ESRD after living-donor kidney transplantation induces quantitative and qualitative modifications of the fecal microbiota, and that specific microbial signatures are associated with clinical and immunological transplant outcomes. This prospective, single-center, longitudinal, interventional, single-arm cohort study will evaluate microbiota dynamics in 30 adult patients before and after living-donor kidney transplantation. Fecal samples are collected at 14 days before transplantation (before immunosuppression), the day before transplantation (after 4 days of immunosuppression), and 3 months post-transplantation. Urinary samples are collected at transplantation. Blood samples (serum, plasma, PBMCs) are collected at 3 timepoints for immunological and metabolomic analyses. The primary endpoint is to describe fecal microbiota beta-diversity dynamics (Bray-Curtis and Jaccard indices at genus level) across three timepoints. Secondary objectives evaluate associations between microbiota composition and clinical outcomes (rejection, infection, survival), immunosuppressant tolerance, drug levels, PBMC immunological profiles, metabolomic signatures, and dietary patterns.
primary_outcomes: Change in Fecal Microbiota Beta-Diversity (Bray-Curtis and Jaccard Indices) at the Genus Taxonomic Level
Change in Fecal Microbiota Beta-Diversity (Bray-Curtis and Jaccard Indices) at the Genus Taxonomic Level
Change in Fecal Microbiota Beta-Diversity (Bray-Curtis and Jaccard Indices) at the Genus Taxonomic Level
title: Microbiota Changes Related to Outcomes in Kidney Transplantation

brief_summary:
The goal of this pilot randomized controlled trial is to compare the effectiveness of focused extracorporeal shockwave therapy (ESWT) versus radial ESWT on gastrocnemius spasticity in children with spastic quadriplegic cerebral palsy (CP). The main questions it aims to answer are:

1. Does focused ESWT (fESWT) reduce gastrocnemius spasticity more effectively than radial ESWT (rESWT)?
2. Are the antispastic effects of fESWT more durable over time compared with rESWT?

Researchers will compare:

* fESWT group (one session weekly, 4 weeks)
* rESWT group (one session weekly, 4 weeks) to see if fESWT more effective to lower Modified Ashworth Scale (MAS) scores during all assessment time points compared with rESWT.

Participants will:

* Be randomly assigned to either fESWT or rESWT group.
* Receive one treatment session per week for 4 consecutive weeks.
* Undergo MAS score evaluations at: baseline, post-intervention weeks 1-4, and follow-up at 4, 8, and 12 weeks after the final treatment.
primary_outcomes: The Modified Ashworth Scale (MAS) score of the gastrocnemius muscle
title: Focused Versus Radial Extracorporeal Shock Wave Therapy on Gastrocnemius Spasticity in Children With Spastic Quadriplegic Cerebral Palsy

brief_summary:
The goal of this randomized, double-blind clinical trial is to evaluate the effects of a single session of manual acupuncture on superoxide dismutase (SOD) enzyme activity and smoking cravings in active smokers aged 21-40 years. The study will also examine the correlation between changes in SOD enzyme activity and changes in smoking cravings, as measured by the Questionnaire of Smoking Urges-Brief (QSU-Brief).

The main questions it aims to answer are:

1. Does a single session of manual acupuncture increase SOD enzyme activity, an indicator of antioxidant defense, 90 minutes after the intervention?
2. Does a single session of manual acupuncture reduce smoking cravings as measured by the Questionnaire of Smoking Urges-Brief (QSU-Brief)?
3. Is there a correlation between changes in SOD enzyme activity and changes in QSU-Brief scores?

Researchers will compare a manual acupuncture group with a sham acupuncture group to determine whether manual acupuncture produces greater changes in SOD enzyme activity and smoking cravings.

Participants will:

1. Be randomly assigned to receive either one 30-minute session of manual acupuncture or sham acupuncture.
2. Refrain from smoking for two hours before the intervention until the final blood sample is collected.
3. Undergo venous blood sampling before the intervention and 90 minutes after the intervention to measure SOD enzyme activity.
4. Complete the QSU-Brief questionnaire before and immediately after the intervention to assess changes in smoking cravings.
primary_outcomes: Change in Superoxide Dismutase (SOD) Enzyme Activity
title: The Effects of Manual Acupuncture on Superoxide Dismutase Enzyme Activity and Questionnaire of Smoking Urges-Brief Scores in Active Smokers: A Randomized Controlled Trial

brief_summary:
The goal of this prospective registry cohort study is to evaluate the efficacy and quality-of-life impact of ablation therapy in patients with non-puerperal mastitis. The main questions it aims to answer are:

Does ablation therapy effectively control inflammation in patients with non-puerperal mastitis?

Does ablation therapy lead to a superior quality of life compared to standard treatments?

Researchers will compare patients receiving ablation therapy to those receiving oral medication or surgery to see if ablation provides better inflammatory control and improves patients' quality of life.

Participants will undergo their assigned treatment (ablation, oral medication, or surgery) and be asked to complete regular follow-up visits and quality-of-life questionnaires over a long-term period.
title: Ablation Versus Non-ablation Strategies for Non-puerperal Mastitis: A Prospective Real-world Registry Study

brief_summary:
Researchers are looking for new ways to treat rheumatoid arthritis (RA). Methotrexate (MTX) is a standard (usual) treatment for RA. However, MTX and other current treatments may not work well to treat RA symptoms for many people. Researchers are doing this trial to learn if a trial medicine called MK-8690 can treat symptoms of active RA in people who are taking MTX.

The goal of this study is to learn if MK-8690 works better than placebo to improve RA symptoms.
primary_outcomes: Percentage of Participants Achieving American College of Rheumatology 50% Response Criteria (ACR50) at Week 12
title: A Clinical Trial of MK-8690 in Participants With Rheumatoid Arthritis (MK-8690-004)

brief_summary:
The goal of this trial is to determine safe dosing of CD19-CD34t metabolically programmed CAR-T cell therapy in adult patients with CD19-positive B-cell acute lymphocytic leukemia (B-ALL).

The main questions it aims to answer are to determine the maximum tolerated dose (MTD) of CD19-CD34t metabolically programmed CAR-T cell therapy, to assess the safety of CD19-CD34t metabolically programmed CAR-T cell therapy, and to determine the feasibility of manufacturing CD19-CD34t metabolically programmed CAR-T cell therapy within 15% of the target dose.
primary_outcomes: Determine the maximum tolerated dose (MTD) of CD19-CD34t metabolically programmed CAR-T cell therapy in adult patients with CD19-positive B-cell acute lymphocytic leukemia (B-ALL).
Assess the safety of CD19-CD34t metabolically programmed CAR-T cell therapy
Determine the feasibility of manufacturing CD19-CD34t metabolically programmed CAR-T cell therapy within 15% of the target dose.
title: Metabolically Fit CD19 CAR T Cells With CD34 Selection Markers in Adults With CD19-Positive B-Cell Acute Lymphocytic Leukemia

brief_summary:
High blood pressure is a major risk factor for atrial fibrillation (AF), an irregular heart rhythm, and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), a condition in which the heart becomes stiff and cannot relax properly. Both conditions can significantly affect quality of life and frequently occur together. In individuals with high blood pressure, increased activity of the nerves surrounding the kidneys can further elevate blood pressure and contribute to strain on the heart.

Renal denervation (RDN) is a procedure designed to lower blood pressure by reducing the activity of these nerves using a thin catheter and controlled energy. RDN has been shown to lower blood pressure safely in many patients; however, the potential benefits in individuals with concurrent AF and HFpEF remain uncertain.

This pilot study will be conducted in two phases. Phase 1 will assess the safety and feasibility of accessing the renal arteries and evaluating blood pressure responses to brief electrical stimulation of the renal nerves.
conditions: Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction (HFPEF)
interventions: Catheter-based renal artery electrical stimulation (as a feasibility assessment for renal denervation)
primary_outcomes: Technical Success Rate of Renal Artery Cannulationn
Change in Invasive Arterial Blood Pressure During Renal Artery Stimulation
title: Renal Denervation in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation and Hypertension

brief_summary:
This study evaluated whether using several monitoring methods together during general anesthesia could improve patient safety and help anesthesiologists adjust medication doses in adults undergoing ear, nose, and throat (ENT) surgery.

The study included 200 adult patients at a university hospital in Palermo, Italy. Patients were assigned alternately to one of two groups. One group received standard monitoring together with additional monitoring of anesthesia depth (BIS), responses to surgical stimulation (SPI), and muscle relaxation (TOF). The other group received standard monitoring alone. Group assignment followed a fixed alternating sequence rather than random selection.

The researchers compared the amount of anesthetic medication used during surgery and the occurrence of anesthesia-related complications during the first 48 hours after surgery, including delayed recovery of breathing, nausea and vomiting, shivering, and residual muscle weakness.

The study was conducted between February and December 2025 and has been completed.
title: Multimodal Monitoring During General Anesthesia in ENT Surgery

brief_summary:
\*\*Brief Summary\*\*

Glaucoma is a progressive eye disease that can lead to irreversible vision loss if intraocular pressure (IOP) is not adequately controlled. Some patients with advanced glaucoma require surgery when medications and/or laser treatment fail to achieve the desired pressure reduction.

This prospective, single-center interventional study aims to evaluate the short-term effectiveness and safety of a combined glaucoma surgery involving deep sclerectomy, trabeculotomy. The study will include 20 eyes of eligible adult patients with advanced glaucoma who require surgical treatment to lower intraocular pressure.

All participants will undergo the planned surgical procedure and receive postoperative care according to a standardized protocol. Follow-up examinations will be performed on the first postoperative day, at one week, and at one, three, and six months after surgery.

The primary outcome will be the change in intraocular pressure from baseline to three months after surgery. Secondary outcomes will include changes in the number of glaucoma medications required, visual acuity, surgical success, the need for additional treatment, and the occurrence of intraoperative or postoperative complications.

The findings are expected to provide information about the short-term effectiveness and safety of this modified surgical technique in patients with advanced glaucoma. As a single-center study without a comparison group, the results will be interpreted in the context of its design and sample size.
conditions: Deep Sclerectomy With Trabeculotomy in Advanced Glaucoma
primary_outcomes: Change in Intraocular Pressure from Baseline to 3 Months After Surger
title: Short-Term Efficacy and Safety of Combined Deep Sclerectomy With Trabeculotomy in Advanced Glaucoma: A Prospective Interventional Study

brief_summary: This single-center prospective randomized controlled trial plans to recruit 60 adult patients with recurrent ascending cholangitis after biliary-enteric anastomosis. Subjects will be randomized 1:1 to the intervention group or control group. The control group receives standard treatment. The intervention group takes rifaximin tablets together with standard treatment for 3 months. We will follow participants for 3 months. The primary outcome is the number of recurrent biliary infections. We will also evaluate gut microbiota changes and adverse events. This open-label study explores whether rifaximin can lower the recurrence risk of cholangitis after biliary-enteric anastomosis.
conditions: Recurrent Ascending Cholangitis After Biliary-enteric Anastomosis
primary_outcomes: Number of recurrent episodes of retrograde biliary infection within 3 months
title: Rifaximin for Prevention of Recurrent Mild-to-moderate Ascending Cholangitis After Biliary-enteric Anastomosis

brief_summary: This cross-sectional observational study aims to investigate the correlation between trunk muscle endurance and dynamic balance in patients with sacroiliac joint dysfunction (SIJD). Trunk muscle endurance will be assessed using standardized clinical tests (prone isometric chest raise test and trunk flexor endurance test), and dynamic balance will be evaluated using the Biodex Balance System.
title: Correlation Between Trunk Muscles Endurance and Dynamic Balance in Sacroiliac Joint Dysfunction

brief_summary: The study is being conducted to evaluate the efficacy, and safety of SHR-A2009 combined bevacizumab versus Sacituzumab Tirumotecan in the treatment of locally advanced or metastatic non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer
title: SHR-A2009 Combined With Bevacizumab in the Treatment of Locally Advanced or Metastatic Non-squamous Non-small Cell Lung Cancer : a Randomized Controlled, Open, Multicenter Phase III Study

brief_summary:
Congenital hypothyroidism (CH) is a condition present at birth in which the thyroid gland does not produce enough thyroid hormones. These hormones are essential for normal brain development. Although early diagnosis through newborn screening and treatment with thyroid hormone help prevent serious learning difficulties, some children with CH may still experience difficulties with thinking, learning, or development.

This study aims to understand why some children with CH do not achieve the expected level of neurological and cognitive development despite early treatment. The researchers will study 39 patients with CH and compare them with 39 similar individuals without the condition. They will also study 50 children with mild neonatal hyperthyrotropinemia (MNH), a condition involving mildly elevated thyroid-stimulating hormone levels, and compare them with 50 children without the condition.

The study will assess medical information, growth measurements, and cognitive test results. Genetic testing will be used to identify changes in genes that may affect thyroid function or brain development. The researchers will also examine chemical changes that regulate how genes work, known as epigenetic changes, and analyze blood samples to identify differences in substances involved in the body's metabolism.

By combining these findings, the study aims to identify factors associated with less favorable developmental outcomes and potential markers that may help identify children at risk. The results may improve understanding of congenital thyroid disorders and support earlier recognition of children who may need additional assessment or individualized care.
primary_outcomes: Genetic mechanisms associated with neurological and cognitive outcomes in patients with congenital hypothyroidism
Association of epigenetic and metabolomic profiles with neurological and cognitive outcomes
title: Understanding the Subnormal Rescue ofNeurological Development in Congenital Hypothyroidism (2022E5SZEM)

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to determine whether women who engage in heavy drinking with a history of sexual assault (SA) victimization show heightened baseline reactivity to uncertain threat (U-threat), whether alcohol reduces this reactivity and related anxiety, and how these processes link to real-world drinking behavior. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Test whether heavy drinking women with a history of SA display exaggerated baseline reactivity to U-threat.
* In the lab, test whether alcohol intoxication is associated with decreases in reactivity to U-threat and subjective anxiety, particularly in heavy drinking women with a history of SA.
* In the real-world, test associations between SA victimization, reactivity to U-threat, alcohol consumption, and anxiolytic relief.

Participants will:

* Complete a screening and orientation session
* Complete two experimental lab sessions that will include intravenous (IV) administration of either 80mg% alcohol or placebo (saline), order counterbalanced
* Complete daily ecological momentary assessments (EMA) surveys for 21 days
* Wear a transdermal alcohol wrist biosensor (BACTrack Skyn) for 21-days
primary_outcomes: Startle eyeblink potentiation during the threat task
Subjective affective response to alcohol in the lab
Subjective effects of alcohol in the lab
Ecological momentary assessment (EMA) of affective response to alcohol in the real world
title: Examining the Role of Sensitivity to Uncertain Threat and Alcohol Response in Risk for Alcohol Use Disorder Following Sexual Assault in College Women

brief_summary: Most people turn first to primary care when they experience emotional distress. Mental health stigma can influence how symptoms are understood, the care people receive, and the trust between professionals and patients. ODISSEA is a pilot study that will co-create and test a practical training intervention designed to help primary care teams reduce mental health stigma in everyday practice. The program combines brief narratives from people with lived experience of mental health problems, guided reflection, and practical digital or audiovisual materials adapted to busy primary care settings. The intervention will be implemented in at least six primary care centers, and changes in mental health-related attitudes, practice-oriented knowledge, and perceived usefulness will be assessed. Focus groups with professionals and interviews with people with lived experience will explore perceived usefulness, needed adaptations, barriers, facilitators, and opportunities for improvement. The results will support the development of an optimized and transferable training package for potential integration into continuing professional education within the Catalan health system and scientific societies.
interventions: Multicomponent anti-stigma educational intervention for primary care professionals
lead_sponsor: Fundacio d'Investigacio en Atencio Primaria Jordi Gol i Gurina
primary_outcomes: Acceptability and satisfaction assessed with the Client Satisfaction Questionnaire (CSQ-8)
title: Pilot Study to Co-create and Implement a Multicomponent Intervention to Reduce Mental Health Stigma in Primary Care

brief_summary:
Some people develop erythrocytosis, a condition characterized by having too many red blood cells, because of inherited changes (mutations) in genes such as EPAS1, EGLN1, or VHL. These genes are involved in the body's oxygen-sensing pathway and can cause the body to produce excess red blood cells. High red blood cell counts can increase the risk of symptoms and complications, including headaches, blood clots, and cardiovascular problems.

This study will evaluate whether belzutifan, a medication that blocks the activity of HIF-2α, can reduce red blood cell production and improve blood counts in patients with erythrocytosis caused by these genetic mutations. Participants will receive belzutifan and undergo regular clinical assessments and laboratory testing to monitor treatment response and safety. The results of this study may provide a new targeted treatment option for patients with hereditary erythrocytosis caused by abnormalities in the oxygen-sensing pathway.
title: Phase IIA Study of Belzutifan in EPAS1-, EGLN1-, or VHL-Mutant Erythrocytosis

brief_summary: A phase 1/2, two-part trial consisting of an open label dose-escalation part and a randomized, double blind, placebo-controlled part to investigate safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and efficacy with EDIT-401 gene editing in adult male and female participants 18 to 65 years of age who require additional lowering of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) such as those with clinical diagnosis of Heterozygous Familial Hypercholesterolemia (HeFH).
primary_outcomes: Part 1: Incidence of treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) and serious adverse events (SAEs)
Part 2: Placebo-controlled percent change from baseline in serum LDL-C
title: EDIT-401 in Adults Who Require Additional Lowering of Low-Density Lipoprotein Cholesterol (LDL-C)

brief_summary: Breast cancer is considered the most common type of malignancies, it is the most frequently diagnosed representing around 2.3 million cases. Where, their chemotherapy may cause fatigue affecting the overall quality of patient's life. Gait and balance are fundamental for activities of daily living and maintaining functional independence.
title: Gait Parameters in Breast Cancer Receiving Chemotherapy Patients

brief_summary:
Prehospital end-of-life care presents complex clinical, ethical, relational, and organizational challenges for healthcare professionals working in the Strasbourg Mobile Emergency and Resuscitation Service (SMUR). A comfort care booklet was introduced in the service in March 2025 to harmonize practices and improve the quality of palliative care delivered in the prehospital setting. However, professionals' experiences, perceptions of the booklet, its perceived impact on practice, and their needs have not yet been explored.

This qualitative descriptive study will explore the experiences, perceptions, and needs of SMUR healthcare professionals regarding prehospital end-of-life care and the implementation of the comfort care booklet. Individual semi-structured face-to-face interviews will be conducted, audio-recorded, transcribed anonymously, and analyzed using an inductive thematic approach. Approximately 12 to 20 participants will be recruited through purposive sampling, with recruitment continuing until data saturation is reached.
primary_outcomes: Data saturation regarding perceptions of prehospital end-of-life care and use of the comfort care booklet
title: Prehospital Care of End-of-Life Patients by the Strasbourg Mobile Emergency and Resuscitation Service: A Qualitative Study of Healthcare Professionals' Experiences and Use of a Comfort Care Booklet

brief_summary: This study evaluates the effect of an ultrasound-guided posterior cutaneous nerve of the forearm epicondylar branch block on pain and functional status in patients with lateral epicondylitis. The procedure is performed using ultrasound guidance. Pain and elbow function are assessed before and after the intervention to determine whether this nerve block can improve pain and functional outcomes in patients with lateral epicondylitis.
interventions: Conventional therapy (home exercise program and epicondylitis band)
lead_sponsor: Gaziler Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation Education and Research Hospital
title: Effect of Ultrasound-Guided Posterior Cutaneous Nerve of the Forearm Epicondylar Branch Block on Pain and Function in Lateral Epicondylitis (PCNF-BrEpi)

brief_summary: Pneumonia is a major public health concern globally and domestically. Dyspnea experienced by hospitalized pneumonia patients often induces anxiety and psychological distress. Wintergreen essential oil, primarily composed of methyl salicylate, is commonly used for comfort care and respiratory relief. This study aims to evaluate the effects of wintergreen essential oil inhalation on dyspnea, physiological parameters, laboratory data, pulmonary function, and subjective comfort in hospitalized pneumonia patients.
title: The Effects of Wintergreen Essential Oil Inhalation on Alleviating Dyspnea Among Patients With Pneumonia

brief_summary: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial that included 28 healthy volunteers allocated to four experimental single dose groups (n = 7 per group) (ayahuasca 0.5 mL/kg, 1.0 mL/kg, 1.5 mL/kg, or placebo)
primary_outcomes: Personality assessments (primary outcome) were conducted at baseline and at a 21-day follow-up using the NEO Five-Factor Inventory-Revised (NEO-FFI-R)
title: Effects of Different Doses of Ayahuasca on Personality in Healthy Volunteers

brief_summary: During this first phase of the study, the investigators are conducting focus group to conduct a needs assessment. Specifically, the investigators will be holding focus groups with adolescents with ADHD as well as separate focus groups with the adolescents' parents to better understand the current needs of youth with ADHD and how to best support them.
title: Phase 1: Thrive Together

brief_summary: This study is a open-label, multicenter clinical trials. The target population is participants with locally advanced or metastatic solid tumors. A total of 204 participants are planned to be included.
primary_outcomes: The occurrence and frequency of Treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs)
The occurrence and frequency of Dose-limiting toxicities (DLTs) DLTs during the study
Objective remission rate (ORR) assessed by the investigator according to RECIST v1.1
title: A Study to Evaluate YF550 in Participants With Locally Advanced or Metastatic Solid Tumors.

brief_summary:
One treatment for treatment-refractory OCD is a procedure called anterior capsulotomy, which modifies a part of the brain called the anterior limb of the internal capsule (ALIC). The ALIC contains connections between some regions of the brain that are overactive in OCD. Anterior capsulotomy can be done with a minimally invasive procedure called radiosurgery, which uses a one-time targeted radiation treatment to weaken the hyperactive connections that travel through the ALIC.

Traditionally, radiosurgery was done using a machine called the Gamma Knife. Many radiation treatment centers use a different type of treatment machine, called a linear accelerator, to treat conditions in the brain that were traditionally treated on the Gamma Knife.

This study will enroll 10 patients and offer anterior capsulotomy on a linear accelerator radiosurgery system and monitor participants OCD symptom improvement after the procedure. This study will also use a special type of brain imaging technique, called task-based functional MRI, to collect information about brain activity before and after treatment.
primary_outcomes: Change is Yale-Brown Obsessive Compulsive Scale (Y-BOSC) score
title: Linear Accelerator Radiosurgical Anterior Capsulotomy With Task-based fMRI Identification of PERSonalized and PrEdictiVE Biomarkers of REsponse in Treatment-Refractory Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder (PERSEVERE Trial)

brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to compare latency (prolongation of pregnancy from diagnosis till delivery) in patients with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) with severe features \< 34 weeks gestational age (GA), undergoing expectant management between tight and permissive blood pressure (BP) groups.
interventions: Treating BP acutely with intravenous or rapid acting oral medications
primary_outcomes: Mean latency from diagnosis of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) to delivery (continuous, mean with standard deviation)
title: Blood Pressure Goal in Preterm Preeclampsia

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if a chin strap helps reduce low oxygen episodes in premature babies receiving CPAP or NIPPV (breathing support through the nose). The main question it aims to answer is:

Does wearing a chin strap during CPAP or NIPPV make low oxygen episodes shorter compared to not wearing one?

Researchers will compare the chin strap period to the no-chin-strap period to see if the chin strap shortens low oxygen episodes.

Participants will:

Be randomly assigned to wear the chin strap first or skip it first Wear a soft chin strap for 24 hours, then switch to no chin strap for 24 hours (or the reverse), with a 1-hour break in between Have continuous monitoring of oxygen levels, heart rate, and breathing throughout the 49-hour study
title: Strap To Reduce Apnea in Preterm Infants: A Randomized Crossover Trial

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn which drug amongst Amoxicillin, Clindamycin and Azithromycin single dose works better in reducing post-surgical complications in Participants getting lower wisdom teeth pulled. The main question it aims to answer is:

• Which single dose drug lowers the post-surgical complications in participants of this study? Researcher will compare three single dose drugs (the administration of the complete amount of an antibiotic medication in one single administration to cure or prevent an infection).

Participants will:

* Take provided drug one hour before the treatment
* Visit the OPD for Reading measurements same day before the surgery, same day after the surgery and third day after the surgery.
primary_outcomes: No. of Participants with Dry Socket
No. of Participants with Surgical Site Infection
title: Comparison of Amoxicillin, Clindamycin and Azithromycin Single Doses Antibiotic Prophylaxis in Patient Undergoing Lower Third Molar Extraction

brief_summary:
This is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, decentralized clinical trial evaluating the effects of MN Nutra GeLiPthin-1™, a multi-ingredient dietary supplement, on body weight, BMI, waist circumference, appetite, satiety, and energy levels in overweight and obese adults over six weeks. A total of 170 generally healthy adults aged 18-65 years with a BMI of 27.0-35.0 kg/m² will be randomized 1:1 to receive either the active supplement or a matching placebo.

Participants will take three capsules orally twice daily for six weeks. All study activities are conducted remotely, including electronic consent, self-administered anthropometric measurements using a sponsor-provided Withings Scale and tape measure, and weekly online questionnaires via the Citruslabs digital study platform. The primary outcome is change in body weight from Baseline to Week 6.
title: A Study to Evaluate the Effects of a Dietary Supplement on Weight Management and Appetite Control

brief_summary:
People who receive an allogeneic stem cell transplant often face important physical and emotional challenges during their recovery. Even after leaving the hospital, they may experience symptoms such as fatigue, pain, anxiety, uncertainty, or difficulties returning to their usual daily activities. Family caregivers may also experience a considerable burden during this period.

Palliative care is specialized supportive care aimed at improving quality of life for people facing serious illness. It focuses on helping patients and families manage symptoms, cope with emotional and practical challenges, and receive care that is aligned with their needs and priorities. While palliative care is increasingly integrated into cancer care, it is not routinely offered to all patients recovering from stem cell transplantation.

The COMPAS study aims to determine whether it is feasible and acceptable to systematically offer palliative care consultations to patients after allogeneic stem cell transplantation. Participants will receive supportive consultations with a palliative care physician in addition to their usual transplant follow-up care.

The study will evaluate whether patients are willing to participate, whether the consultations can be delivered as planned, and how patients and caregivers perceive this approach. Participants and caregivers will also be invited to complete questionnaires and some may take part in interviews about their experience.

The results of this study will help determine whether a larger future study should be conducted and may contribute to improving supportive care for people recovering from stem cell transplantation.
title: Comprehensive Palliative Care After Stem Cell Transplantation: a Feasability Study

brief_summary: This is a retrospective, multicenter observational study evaluating the clinical value of combining high-resolution (1024×1024 matrix) targeted CT scans with an artificial intelligence (AI) deep learning system to distinguish between benign and malignant pulmonary nodules. By analyzing existing medical records and CT images of adult patients (aged 18 and older) with pulmonary nodules (3-30 mm) who have confirmed diagnoses (via postoperative pathology）, this study aims to assess the diagnostic accuracy and efficiency of the AI system. The study plans to enroll approximately 10,000 cases from three hospitals in Shanghai. The primary goal is to evaluate the AI system's diagnostic performance (such as sensitivity, specificity, and Area Under the ROC Curve) and compare it with the performance of radiologists, ultimately exploring whether this combined approach can provide more accurate clinical diagnoses and reduce unnecessary procedures.
primary_outcomes: The Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUC) for AI Model Diagnosis of Pulmonary Nodules
title: Clinical Application of Artificial Intelligence Methods in Diagnostic Imaging of Pulmonary Nodules

brief_summary: Ureteral stones are a common condition, especially small and distal stones, and can cause renal colic pain. Medical expulsive therapy (MET) is widely used to facilitate stone passage. In this prospective, non-randomized, controlled study, the effect of acupuncture administered in addition to MET on the spontaneous passage of ureteral stones will be evaluated. A total of 40 patients with ureteral stones are planned to be included in the study. Patients will be followed in two groups: MET and acupuncture administered in addition to MET. During the ten-day follow-up period, the stone passage rate, time to stone passage, pain severity, and need for analgesic use will be evaluated. The aim of the study is to investigate the effect of adding acupuncture to MET on ureteral stone passage and symptoms.
title: The Effect of Acupuncture on Passing Ureteral Stones

brief_summary: This split-mouth randomized controlled clinical trial evaluates and compares the clinical and radiographic success of Dia-Root Bio MTA versus conventional Mineral Trioxide Aggregate (MTA Plus) as indirect pulp capping (IPC) materials in young permanent molars.
interventions: Dia-Root Bio MTA Indirect Pulp Capping
primary_outcomes: Radiographic Success Rate and Dentin Bridge Formation
title: Clinical and Radiographic Evaluation of Dia-Root Bio MTA for Indirect Pulp Capping in Young Permanent Molars

brief_summary:
Purpose: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the acceptability of field-based long acting cabotegravir/rilpivirine (LA-CAB/RPV) among people with HIV (PWH) who are out of care.

Participants: 40 adult men and women living with HIV will be enrolled

Procedures (methods): This is a pilot, open-label study to evaluate the acceptability, feasibility, and virologic impact of field-based LA-CAB-RPV for PWH who are out of care. This study will enroll 40 participants who accept field-based LA-CAB-RPV, targeting \>50% who reside in rural or semi-rural counties. Participants will be followed for 7 months, with duration of follow-up selected based on the FDA approved every 2 month LA-CAB-RPV injection schedule for virally suppressed patients, aligning with the 5th injection for an every two-month cycle
lead_sponsor: University of North Carolina, Chapel Hill
primary_outcomes: Percent of preliminarily eligible participants who accept and receive field-based injection (acceptability)
Percentage of participants who receive all indicated LA-CAB/RPV injections within the allowable 14-day window (feasibility)
title: Reaching Persons With HIV Who Are Out of Care Through Expedited Access to Long-Acting Injectable Antiretroviral Therapy - The RELAI Study

brief_summary:
The Primary Objective of this study is to evaluate the efficacy and safety of teniposide in combination with temozolomide for the treatment of newly diagnosed glioblastoma (nGBM) with MGMT promotor region unmethylated.

The study will also assess the safety of teniposide combined with temozolomide. The primary questions to be addressed include:

* Does the treatment demonstrate efficacy for the disease under study?
* What medical problems or adverse events may participants experience while receiving the study drugs?

Participants will:

* Receive teniposide: 60 mg/m² in 500 mL of normal saline, administered as an intravenous infusion over at least 30 minutes, once daily on Days 1-3 of each cycle. Each cycle is 28 days, for a total of 6 cycles.Receive temozolomide (TMZ) orally: 150 mg/m² once daily for 5 days during Cycle 1; starting from Cycle 2, the dose will be increased to 200 mg/m² once daily for 5 days. Each cycle is 28 days, for a total of 6 cycles.
* Visit the hospital for assessments at each cycle.
* Have their medication adherence and assessment results recorded.
title: A Single-Arm, Open-Label, Multicenter Clinical Study of Teniposide Combined With Temozolomide for the Treatment of Newly Diagnosed Glioblastoma (nGBM) With MGMT Promotor Region Unmethylated

brief_summary: This is a phase 2b, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, dose-ranging,14-day dosing, 2-period crossover study in participants with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).
primary_outcomes: Bronchodilation - time to onset of FEV1 >100mL
title: Phase 2b Efficacy and Safety Study of AERO-007, an Inhaled LABA+LAMA Combination for Nebulization Delivery in COPD Patients

brief_summary: This study will compare a 15-minute back massage, 15 minutes of quiet rest, and no additional break before a mental task in healthy adults aged 18 to 27 years. Each participant will complete all three conditions in a random order at separate visits. The study will measure task accuracy, heart rate, skin conductance, and perceived workload to assess whether massage offers a benefit beyond rest.
title: Back Massage Before a Cognitive Task in Healthy Young Adults

brief_summary:
Uterine fibroids are the most common benign tumors in women of reproductive age and are a major indication for hysterectomy. This retrospective, single-center observational study aims to identify factors associated with the success or failure of vaginal natural orifice transluminal endoscopic surgery (v-NOTES) hysterectomy for large and very large uteri.

Approximately 50 adult women who underwent v-NOTES hysterectomy for a large uterus at Strasbourg University Hospitals between January 1, 2024, and December 31, 2025, will be included. Data will be extracted retrospectively from medical records. The primary outcome is successful completion of the v-NOTES procedure without conversion to another surgical approach. Potential predictive factors include body mass index, parity, uterine weight, fibroid location, adenomyosis, vaginal access, previous cesarean deliveries or pelvic surgery, and preoperative medical treatments intended to reduce uterine volume or inflammation.

Secondary outcomes include surgical complications, operative duration, length of hospital stay, and unplanned readmission within 30 days of surgery.
conditions: Vaginal Natural Orifice Transluminal Endoscopic Surgery (v-NOTES)
primary_outcomes: Successful completion of v-NOTES hysterectomy without conversion to another surgical approach
title: Predictors of Success and Failure of v-NOTES Hysterectomy for Large and Very Large Uteri

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if Quan Duzhong Capsules work to treat primary osteoporosis in adults. It will also learn about the safety of Quan Duzhong Capsules. The main questions it aims to answer are:

Do Quan Duzhong Capsules improve bone mineral density (BMD) of the lumbar spine (L1-L4) after 6 months of treatment?

Do Quan Duzhong Capsules change muscle strength, the number of falls, and bone metabolism markers?

What medical problems do participants have when taking Quan Duzhong Capsules?

Researchers will compare Quan Duzhong Capsules to a placebo (a look-alike substance that contains no drug) to see if Quan Duzhong Capsules work to treat primary osteoporosis. Both groups will also take a calcium and vitamin D3 preparation.

Participants will:

Take Quan Duzhong Capsules or a placebo 3 capsules twice daily after meals, plus 1 calcium and vitamin D3 tablet once daily 10 minutes after dinner, for 6 months

Visit the clinic at baseline and after 6 months for checkups and tests, including bone mineral density (DXA) scans and blood tests for bone metabolism, calcium and phosphorus metabolism, liver and kidney function

Report any falls, symptoms, and medical problems during the study
lead_sponsor: Shanghai University of Traditional Chinese Medicine
primary_outcomes: Change in bone mineral density (BMD) of the lumbar spine (L1-L4)

brief_summary:
Each year, approximately 1,000 patients in the Netherlands are diagnosed with liver cancer. When liver cancer can no longer be treated with surgery or thermal ablation, cure is no longer possible. In recent years, immunotherapy has become increasingly important in the treatment of liver cancer. Unfortunately, the combination of immunotherapy (atezolizumab) and an anti-angiogenic agent (bevacizumab) results in a durable response in only 15-20% of patients. The aim of this study is to identify a strategy to enhance the effectiveness of immunotherapy, enabling the patient's immune system to better recognize and attack the cancer.

Two recent clinical observations suggested that the immune system may be activated by external radiotherapy or radioembolization. Following these treatments, both patients unexpectedly showed regression of multiple non-irradiated liver metastases. One of these patients had initially experienced disease progression during immunotherapy, but after radiotherapy subsequently demonstrated regression of all metastatic lesions. In this clinical study (16 patients in total), we will investigate whether the immune system can be reactivated after failure of immunotherapy.

Patients will be eligible for participation after disease progression during immunotherapy for liver cancer. In Group A, eight patients will receive three fractions of external radiotherapy directed at the most dominant liver lesion or an extrahepatic metastasis. In Group B, eight patients will receive radioembolization of the most dominant liver lesion. There will be no randomization. Group A will be enrolled first, and Group B will open only after completion of enrollment in Group A.

The primary outcome measure is the number of patients in each group who achieve disease control at 6 months, defined as stable disease or tumor regression lasting for at least 6 months. During the study, participating patients will undergo extensive blood analyses, tumor biopsies of both treated and untreated lesions, and multiple CT scans.

Through these investigations, we aim to characterize the tumor microenvironment in detail, evaluate the role of different immune cell populations, and gain a better understanding of why these treatments administered after immunotherapy failure may still be capable of reactivating the immune system.
title: Overcoming Immunotherapy Resistance in Hepatocellular Carcinoma

brief_summary:
Patients undergoing open posterior lumbar fusion surgery often experience postoperative gastrointestinal problems, such as bloating, constipation, and delayed passage of gas and stool, and may be at nutritional risk. These problems may hinder recovery and prolong hospital stay.

This study enrolled 90 patients undergoing open posterior lumbar fusion surgery at the Department of Orthopedics, First Affiliated Hospital of Kunming Medical University. Participants were randomly assigned in a 1:1:1 ratio to three groups: a control group receiving routine perioperative care with standard dietary guidance; experimental group A receiving perioperative oral nutritional supplements (ONS) together with preoperative and postoperative carbohydrate loading; and experimental group B receiving the same ONS and carbohydrate loading plus a probiotic preparation.

The primary outcome was the length of postoperative hospital stay. Other assessments included time to first postoperative flatus, time to first postoperative bowel movement, cumulative postoperative drainage volume, drainage duration, and time to first postoperative mobilization out of bed. Surgical wound healing, postoperative infections, and overall postoperative complications were assessed during hospitalization and at the outpatient follow-up visit 1 month after surgery. Additional assessments included anthropometric measurements, laboratory tests, and scores evaluating pain, function, nutritional risk, nutritional status, dietary intake, and gastrointestinal function.

Anthropometric measurements were obtained at hospital admission and at the pre-discharge assessment. The Visual Analog Scale (VAS) for overall pain, Japanese Orthopaedic Association (JOA) low back pain score, Nutritional Risk Screening 2002 (NRS-2002), full Mini Nutritional Assessment (MNA), Simple Diet Self-Assessment Tool (SDSAT), and simplified gastrointestinal function score were assessed at hospital admission, on postoperative day 3, at the pre-discharge assessment, and at 1 month after surgery. Laboratory tests were performed before surgery and on postoperative days 1, 3, and 6.

The aim was to evaluate the clinical value of perioperative nutrition management in spinal surgery and explore whether adding probiotics provided further benefit. The study was intended to inform the development of a practical perioperative nutrition management plan to support recovery, shorten hospital stay, and reduce postoperative complications.
lead_sponsor: First Affiliated Hospital of Kunming Medical University
title: Perioperative Nutrition Management in Patients Undergoing Open Posterior Lumbar Surgery

brief_summary:
This study will evaluate the effectiveness of an Information-Motivation-Behavioral Skills (IMB) Model-guided health literacy intervention among adults with hypertension who are non-adherent to prescribed antihypertensive medication. The study will use a cluster randomized controlled trial design in eight public hospitals in North Ethiopia. Four hospitals will be allocated to the intervention group and four to the usual-care control group.

The intervention will address information, motivation, and behavioral skills related to medication adherence and hypertension self-management. Participants in the intervention group will receive the IMB Model-guided health literacy intervention in addition to usual care, while participants in the control group will receive usual care.

The primary outcome is medication adherence. Blood pressure control and other specified hypertension self-management outcomes will be assessed as secondary outcomes. In addition, a qualitative component will explore the perceptions, experiences, and contextual barriers of medication non-adherent hypertensive patients regarding the information, motivation, and behavioral skills that influence their medication adherence and hypertension self-care behaviors.

The study will test the hypothesis that the IMB Model-guided health literacy intervention will improve medication adherence compared with usual care. The qualitative component will provide contextual information to help explain participants' experiences and the factors influencing medication-taking behavior and intervention implementation.
primary_outcomes: Number and proportion of participants adherent to antihypertensive medication, assessed using the four-item Morisky-Green-Levine Medication Adherence Scale
title: IMB-Guided Health Education Intervention for Medication Adherence and Blood Pressure Control in Non-adherent Hypertensive Patients

brief_summary:
Children with severe burns affecting both lower limbs may experience persistent difficulties with balance, walking, and physical function. This randomized controlled trial investigated whether adding progressive hop-stabilization training to standard physical rehabilitation improves postural control, dynamic balance, gait, and lower-limb function.

Fifty-four children aged 10-17 years with healed bilateral lower-limb burns were randomly assigned to two groups. Both groups received standard rehabilitation three times weekly for eight weeks, while the experimental group additionally performed supervised hop-stabilization exercises. Postural stability, dynamic balance, walking ability, and lower-limb functional performance were assessed before and immediately after treatment.
title: Effects of Hop-Stabilization Training on Postural and Functional Rehabilitation in Children With Lower-Limb Burns

brief_summary:

Enrolled children will receive one Hiya Kids Daily Multivitamin chewable tablet administered once daily with the first meal of the day for eight consecutive weeks. Parents or caregivers will complete study-specific questionnaires at Baseline, Week 2, Week 4, Week 6, and Week 8, and a product acceptability assessment at Week 8. All assessments are completed remotely via the study platform. Forty participants will be enrolled.
primary_outcomes: Change in Parent/Caregiver-Perceived Growth and Development

brief_summary:
This study aims to investigate whether combining cycling exercise with an immersive and interactive virtual reality (VR) environment improves motivation compared with cycling without visual support or cycling while watching a route on a television screen in critically ill patients admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU).

This randomized, within-subject crossover study will include 20 adult ICU patients who have been admitted for at least 7 days, have received mechanical ventilation for at least 48 hours, and are able to perform active cycling exercise.

Each participant will complete three 10-minute cycling sessions under different conditions: (1) cycling without visual support (Basic-Cycle), (2) cycling while watching a cycling route on a television screen (TV-Cycle), and (3) cycling within an immersive, interactive VR environment (VR-Cycle). The three conditions will be performed in random order over three consecutive days, with the cycling resistance kept constant across conditions for each participant.

The primary outcome is intrinsic motivation, assessed using the Situational Motivation Scale (SIMS). Secondary outcomes include other dimensions of motivation, perceived dyspnea, lower limb fatigue, pain, cycling distance, and safety measures, including vital signs and adverse events.

This study will provide insight into the potential of VR-assisted cycling to improve patient motivation and engagement during early rehabilitation in the ICU.
title: Cycling Within an Interactive and Immersive Virtual Environment During Critical Illness: a Patient-centred Approach for Lower Limb Rehabilitation

brief_summary: Spasticity is a common consequence of spinal cord injury and can have a profound impact on quality of life. The goal of this study is to learn if an intervention called focused extracorporeal shockwave therapy can enhance the effectiveness of injections received for spasticity, such as Botox. The main questions this study seeks to answer are whether shockwave therapy and toxin injection 1) can improve spasticity symptoms greater than toxin injection alone, and 2) change the structure of the injected muscles. Researchers will compare the group who receives both shockwave therapy and toxin injection to a group who receives only toxin injection. Participants will be asked to visit the clinic five times over the span of three months. The first three visits will occur on three consecutive weeks, during which participants will receive shockwave therapy or the sham therapy. The aim of this study is to evaluate the success rate of revision surgery using a conchal cartilage graft supported with autologous platelet-rich fibrin (PRF), performed under local anesthesia, in patients who previously underwent cartilage tympanoplasty and later developed a recurrent perforation of the graft requiring revision surgery.

In this single-arm prospective study, the perforation will be repaired with a cartilage graft harvested from the concha of the same (previously operated) ear. Both surfaces of the graft will be covered with PRF obtained from the patient's own blood. Patients can be discharged on the same day without systemic antibiotics.

The primary outcome is anatomical success, defined as graft integrity and closure of the perforation. Secondary outcomes include hearing results (air-conduction thresholds and air-bone gap), quality of life (COMQ-12), postoperative pain (VAS), paracetamol use, change in perforation size, complications and operative time. Patients will be followed for 6 months after surgery. A total of 35 patients are planned to be enrolled.

brief_summary:
Writer's cramps (WC) is a focal task-specific upper limb dystonia that significantly impairs handwriting and other manual skills, affecting functionality. WC is one of the most common task-specific dystonias, affecting 3.8-80 per million individuals. The first-line management option is botulinum toxin injections in the muscles affected by the involuntary movements, causing a transient neuromuscular blocking effect and reducing muscle abnormal contraction. However, the effect lasts for around 3 months or less, is invasive, may cause unintended hand weakness, and the benefits are variable in terms of the severity of dystonic contraction and functional gain.

Focal limb dystonia pathophysiology, including writer's cramps, has been linked to propriospinal signalling defects in the sensorimotor cortex modulation5, prompting an investigation into neuromodulation of this region as a modality for dystonia management.

Other forms of dystonia have shown a reduction of the involuntary movements with vibrotactile stimulation (VTS), including cervical and laryngeal dystonia8. These results have supported the hypothesis that VTS alters the abnormal output of mechanical receptors from proprioceptive and tactile pathways to the sensorimotor cortex.Changes in neurophysiological markers of dystonia in the sensorimotor cortex also corroborated the modulatory effect.

Furthermore, more invasive methods of neuromodulation, such as Globus Pallidus internus Deep Brain Stimulation, are known to be an effective treatment option for medically refractory dystonia, with evidence of promoting a similar result on the sensorimotor pathway via cortico-basal ganglia network direct stimulation. Finally, one of the most common ways of modulation is a core feature in dystonia, which is called an alleviating manoeuvre (AM) or geste antagoniste. This comprises a sensory or motor stimulation located in the anatomical area of the dystonia, which will transiently alleviate the involuntary movement. In that case, Functional MRI studies also suggest a sensorimotor network modulation in AM. Thus, there is considerable preliminary evidence to suggest the role of invasive and non-invasive neuromodulation in the treatment of dystonia.

Given the variable and often suboptimal response to standard treatments for task-specific dystonia, such as WC, and the associated functional impairment, this study explores the role of vibrotactile stimulation (VTS) as a non-invasive neuromodulation tool for WC. VTS targets muscles involved in dystonic contractions, intending to create a non-invasive neuromodulation via propriospinal pathways to the sensorimotor cortex and improve motor control in individuals with WC. The effect described in previous studies lasts around 20-30 minutes, which should allow functionality for handwriting during that period of time. In the future, with the refinement of the technique's effectiveness, it could be escalated for a wearable treatment option.

Based on the clinical and pathophysiological characteristics of task-specific dystonia it is reasonable to use a peripheral sensory modulation technique to try and reduced the abnormal motor cortical output this way reducing the dystonic movement. That has been proved successful in other types of dystonia. Thus, a pilot study for proof-of-concept concept and feasibility is a good first step towards that direction.
title: VTS Sensorimotor Neuromodulation in WC

brief_summary:
Pauwels type III femoral neck fractures in young adults commonly result from high-energy trauma and are characterized by a vertical fracture orientation with substantial shear and rotational forces. These fractures are associated with an increased risk of mechanical instability, nonunion, varus collapse, fixation failure, and osteonecrosis of the femoral head. Successful treatment therefore requires anatomical reduction and stable internal fixation capable of resisting both vertical shear and rotational forces.

A Sliding Hip Screw combined with an antirotation screw provides controlled fracture compression and additional rotational stability. Biplane Double Support Screw Fixation is an alternative technique in which cannulated screws are inserted in two planes to provide double cortical support. The distal screw entry points and calcar-supported configuration are intended to distribute axial loading toward the femoral diaphysis, improve mechanical stability, facilitate fracture impaction, and reduce the risk of varus collapse.

This prospective randomized controlled study will compare Biplane Double Support Screw Fixation with Sliding Hip Screw fixation combined with an antirotation screw in young adults with Pauwels type III femoral neck fractures. Participants will be randomly allocated in a 1:1 ratio to receive one of the two fixation techniques.

The study will compare fracture healing, functional recovery, radiological outcomes, and postoperative complications between the two groups. Particular attention will be given to nonunion, osteonecrosis of the femoral head, varus collapse, implant failure, and the need for additional surgery. The study hypothesis is that Biplane Double Support Screw Fixation may provide stable fixation with clinical and radiological outcomes comparable or superior to those achieved using a Sliding Hip Screw with an antirotation screw.
interventions: Dynamic Hip Screw with Anterotation Screw Fixation
primary_outcomes: Functional outcome assessed using the Harris Hip Score was evaluated and calculated at each follow-up visit, with the mean value presented
Rate of osteonecrosis of the femoral head
title: BDSF Vs DHS With Anterotational Screw in Vertical FNF

Currently, no standardized screening test is routinely used by all healthcare professionals in France to identify PFD, despite its reported prevalence and potential consequences for child development, family well-being, and healthcare costs.

The D-TAP questionnaire will be compared with the Montreal Children's Hospital Feeding Scale. A blinded clinical speech-language pathology assessment of information collected during a semi-structured parental interview will be used to identify signs suggestive of PFD.

A total of 100 children will be included. The study will assess the diagnostic performance of the D-TAP questionnaire, identify an optimal screening threshold, and explore whether parents initiate contact with a community-based speech-language therapist within six weeks after being informed of signs suggestive of PFD.
conditions: Feeding Difficulties in Infants and Young Children

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to learn whether dexmedetomidine nasal spray is associated with a lower risk of postoperative sore throat in adult patients who underwent bronchoscopy under general anesthesia. The main questions it aims to answer are:

Is dexmedetomidine nasal spray associated with a lower incidence of sore throat after bronchoscopy? What is the average treatment effect of dexmedetomidine nasal spray on postoperative sore throat? Does the treatment effect differ across patient subgroups (treatment effect heterogeneity)? Researchers will compare patients who received dexmedetomidine nasal spray with patients who did not receive it to see if the nasal spray is associated with less postoperative sore throat, and whether some patients benefit more than others.

This is a two-center retrospective cohort study. No participants will be asked to do anything, and no interventions will be given. Existing medical records of patients who underwent bronchoscopy will be analyzed. The analysis follows a target trial emulation framework, which mimics a randomized trial using existing data, and uses statistical and machine learning methods to account for differences between patient groups.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of Postoperative Sore Throat on Postoperative Day 1
title: Dexmedetomidine Nasal Spray and Postoperative Sore Throat After Bronchoscopy

The main questions this study aims to answer are: Does PULSAR improve overall survival compared with BSC? Does PULSAR delay deterioration in patient-reported outcomes and quality of life compared with BSC? Can adaptive radiotherapy delivered in ultrafractionated pulses improve the therapeutic ratio in patients with HCC and poor liver function? The study will compare PULSAR with BSC to evaluate differences in survival, disease control, liver function, and treatment-related toxicity. Participants in the BSC arm will receive standard supportive care. All participants will undergo regular assessments of survival, disease progression, liver function, toxicities, and quality of life.

brief_summary: As life expectancy increases, the rate of disability among elderly individuals is also rising. Elderly patients undergoing home-based rehabilitation after surgery without medical supervision may experience complications and adverse events such as nausea, vomiting, or bleeding, which can impair recovery of daily living functions and commonly lead to readmission after discharge-particularly in older adults with multiple comorbidities, declining physical function, or cognitive impairment, who face a higher risk. Postoperative neurocognitive disorder (PND) is common following anesthesia and surgery, affecting up to 65% of adults aged 65 and older, and is associated with significant morbidity and mortality. Most patients do not undergo baseline or follow-up neuropsychological testing during the perioperative period or afterward, limiting the identification and early intervention for PND. With increasing life expectancy and a growing number of elderly patients undergoing surgery, the incidence of PND is expected to continue rising, primarily manifesting as declines in memory, attention, information processing, and cognitive flexibility. Current clinical studies suggest that advanced age, low educational level, pre-existing cognitive impairment, and alcohol and/or substance abuse are strong risk factors for developing PND. The perioperative period represents a critical window for identifying and assessing PND.
lead_sponsor: Second Affiliated Hospital of Wenzhou Medical University

brief_summary:
Bacteremia, a common infection associated with high morbidity and mortality, requires prompt and appropriate antibiotic treatment. Numerous studies have shown that the appropriate use of antibiotics helps improve the prognosis of patients, reduce the selection of pathogenic organisms, the emergence of antibiotic resistance, adverse treatment effects, and healthcare costs.

The Nantes University Hospital Center has operated a Biomedical Data Warehouse (BDW) since 2018. The growing availability of data through BDWs thus enables the development of decision-support tools based on machine learning.

The primary objective of the OPTIBact project is to predict the optimal empirical antibiotic for hospitalized patients with bacteremia using a machine learning-based predictive model using data from the Nantes University Hospital's BDW.

As secondary objectives, the study aims:

* To compare the performance of the predictive model for the optimal empirical antibiotic against standard patient care
* To estimate the expected benefit of the predictive model compared to real-world practice in terms of clinical outcomes
* To predict the optimal dosage of empirical antibiotic therapy
* To compare the performance of the predictive model for optimal empirical antibiotic therapy dosing with standard patient care
* To describe inpatient patients in Nantes University Hospital who received optimal antibiotic therapy and those who did not
* To Identify predictors of antibiotic resistance in bacteria isolated from blood cultures, stratified by pathogen type.
title: Predicting the Optimal Empirical Antibiotic Therapy for Bacteremia Using an Artificial Intelligence-based Model
