brief_summary:
Background Tonsillar infections are highly prevalent and are associated with substantial morbidity, including severe sore throat, dysphagia, and general malaise. The disease spectrum ranges from acute tonsillitis (AT) through peritonsillar phlegmon (PP) to peritonsillar abscess (PTA), and clinical data suggest that these conditions often represent a continuum in which inadequate treatment may lead to disease progression.

Traditionally, Group A streptococci have been considered the primary pathogen. However, our previous studies have demonstrated that Fusobacterium necrophorum and Streptococcus dysgalactiae also play important roles in moderate to severe tonsillar infections. The predominant pathogens are susceptible to beta-lactam antibiotics, and in Denmark both oral phenoxymethylpenicillin (PMP) and intravenous benzylpenicillin (BP) are commonly used.

However, PMP exhibits considerable interindividual variability in bioavailability, which may result in insufficient antibiotic exposure. The efficacy of beta-lactam antibiotics depends on the duration that drug concentrations remain above the minimum inhibitory concentration (T\>MIC), and experimental data from our research group have shown that intravenous BP provides more stable and adequate tissue exposure than oral PMP. In clinical practice, rapid symptomatic improvement is often observed following intravenous BP administration, but this has not been investigated in randomized studies.

We hypothesize that a single initial intravenous dose of BP, administered in addition to standard oral PMP therapy, may result in more rapid symptom relief without the need for hospitalization.

Treatment effects will be assessed using disease-specific Patient-Reported Outcome Measures (PROMs), namely the STAT-10 and PTAAT-12 questionnaires, both developed by our research group. The project addresses an important clinical and pharmacological knowledge gap and has the potential to optimize treatment, reduce disease burden, and strengthen outpatient management of tonsillar infections.

Objectives

* To investigate the effects of a single dose of intravenous penicillin as an adjunct to oral penicillin therapy in patients with AT, PP, and PTA, respectively.
* To define the minimal clinically important difference (MCID) for the STAT-10 score and the PTAAT-12 score.

Study Design This is an investigator-initiated, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trial in which patients with AT, PP, or PTA are randomized 1:1 to receive either a single dose of intravenous benzylpenicillin (2 MIU) or placebo (isotonic saline) in addition to standard oral phenoxymethylpenicillin therapy.

Patients will be enrolled into three groups (AT Group, PP Group, and PTA Group), which will be analyzed separately.

Inclusion Criteria Adults (≥18 years of age) with clinically diagnosed acute tonsillitis (AT Group), peritonsillar phlegmon (PP Group), or peritonsillar abscess treated with incision and drainage (PTA Group).

Perspectives The study has the potential to improve the clinical management of patients with AT, PP, and PTA by providing evidence on whether an initial intravenous dose of penicillin enhances treatment outcomes.

Timeline

* Anticipated start of patient recruitment: October 2026.
* Anticipated primary completion: December 2028.
* Anticipated study completion (last participant's 12-month follow-up): December 2029.
title: A Single Dose of Intravenous Penicillin as an Adjunct to Oral Penicillin in the Treatment of Acute Tonsillitis, Peritonsillar Phlegmon, and Peritonsillar Abscess

brief_summary:
The ovarian reserve consists of a finite pool of follicles that gradually declines throughout a woman's reproductive life. During conventional IVF, exogenous gonadotropins are administered for 10-14 days to support the growth and maturation of multiple follicles, followed by induction of final oocyte maturation before oocyte retrieval.

In vitro maturation (IVM) offers an alternative approach in which immature oocytes are retrieved from small antral follicles and matured in the laboratory within 24-44 hours. IVM requires no or only minimal ovarian stimulation and may therefore reduce treatment burden, costs, side effects, and the risk of ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS). Recent advances in the retrieval of oocytes from small antral follicles, together with improved understanding of the molecular mechanisms regulating human oocyte maturation, have renewed interest in IVM and improved its clinical potential.

The overall aim of this project is to implement and optimize IVM as a clinical fertility treatment in Denmark. Specifically, we aim to: (1) evaluate the clinical success rates of IVM compared with conventional IVF; (2) characterize molecular differences between in vivo- and in vitro-matured oocytes and resulting blastocysts, as well as between follicular cells from small antral and preovulatory follicles; and (3) use new insights into the regulation of human oocyte maturation to optimize IVM protocols and improve treatment outcomes. Ultimately, the project aims to establish IVM as a safe, effective, and less burdensome alternative to conventional IVF for selected patient groups.
primary_outcomes: Ratio of blastocyst per metaphase II oocyte
title: Implementing IVM for Fertility Treatment in Clinical Practice

brief_summary:
The goal of this feasibility clinical trial is to learn whether supervised virtual reality (VR) sessions can be safely and practically provided to adults aged 55 years and older with moderate-to-severe dementia who experience agitation while receiving care in inpatient geriatric psychiatry units.

The main questions this study aims to answer are:

Can participants be identified, enrolled, and retained in the study? Can participants tolerate and complete supervised VR sessions? Can clinical staff fit VR sessions into routine inpatient care? What safety or comfort concerns occur during or after VR sessions? Can the study team collect information needed to plan a larger future study?

Following informed consent, prospective participants will undergo screening to determine eligibility. Those who are eligible and enrolled will complete any remaining baseline assessments and will then be offered a brief VR familiarization or orientation procedure. Completion of tolerated familiarization is required before regular VR sessions may begin. Familiarization will not count as intervention initiation or as a regular VR intervention session. These activities form one continuous study period; there is no fixed observational or waiting period.

Participants who tolerate familiarization may be offered supervised VR sessions up to three times per week for up to six weeks, with a maximum of 18 regular sessions. Sessions will start at about 10 minutes and may increase gradually to about 30 minutes, depending on each participant's comfort and tolerance.

Familiarization and early VR exposure will begin with calming, low-stimulation, non-threatening virtual environments. Content may later be adjusted based on the participant's comfort, preferences, observed response, clinical appropriateness, and safety. Participants will remain seated and will be monitored by trained staff. Sessions will not start or will be stopped if the participant shows distress, discomfort, refusal, dizziness, nausea, confusion, worsening agitation, or any other safety concern.

Researchers will also collect information about agitation, behavioural symptoms, quality of life, medication use, staff experience, and workflow. This study is not designed to prove that VR treats agitation or dementia. The findings will be used to determine whether a larger future study is practical and how it should be designed.
conditions: Behavioural and Psychological Symptoms of Dementia
lead_sponsor: London Health Sciences Centre Research Institute OR Lawson Research Institute of St. Joseph's
primary_outcomes: Staff acceptability, appropriateness, usability, implementation feasibility, perceived workload and workflow burden, and workflow integration
title: Virtual Reality to Advance Dementia Care and Quality of Life

brief_summary: Constipation is a common postoperative problem in patients undergoing hip surgery and may be associated with immobilization, opioid analgesic use, and inadequate fluid and fiber intake. Preventive interventions, including adequate fluid and nutritional intake, early mobilization, and abdominal massage, may help maintain bowel function. However, evidence regarding the effectiveness of a standardized checklist to guide and monitor these interventions throughout the perioperative period remains limited. This randomized controlled trial aims to determine the impact of monitoring the risk of perioperative constipation and prevention interventions using a standard checklist on bowel sounds, postoperative constipation severity, and quality of recovery in hip surgery patients. The checklist includes a systematic assessment of constipation risk and monitoring of preventive interventions, including fluid and nutrient intake, early mobilization, and abdominal massage. The findings may contribute to improving perioperative nursing care and constipation prevention in patients undergoing hip surgery.
interventions: Constipation prevention and checklist monitoring in hip surgery patients
title: Effect of a Constipation Prevention Checklist in Hip Surgery Patients

Hence, multiple teeth are affected with dental caries approaching close to pulp. Unfortunately, there is insufficient clinical studies evidence to demonstrate the indirect pulp capping efficacy of the available remineralizing dental materials and the color stability of restorations placed over them over a period of time.

brief_summary: This observational study describes the results of a routine aesthetic treatment for mild to moderate eyebrow drooping (brow ptosis). Thirty-six adults who came to Klinika Estelab (Moscow) asking for rejuvenation of the upper face received, as part of their usual care, one combined treatment session: microfocused ultrasound with visualization (Ultherapy), abobotulinumtoxinA (Dysport) injections, and hyaluronic acid filler in the temples, with a routine toxin touch-up after 2 weeks. The investigators did not assign any treatment; they only added standardized assessments. Eyebrow height was measured on standardized photographs before treatment, immediately after treatment, and at 1, 3, 6, and 12 months. Aesthetic improvement, patient satisfaction, procedural pain, and side effects were also recorded.
primary_outcomes: Change From Baseline in Mean Eyebrow Height
Change From Baseline in Maximum Eyebrow Height
Number of Participants With Adverse Events
title: Single-Session Microfocused Ultrasound, AbobotulinumtoxinA and Temporal Hyaluronic Acid Filler for Non-Surgical Brow Lifting

brief_summary:
Burkitt lymphoma is a rare, highly aggressive B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma in adults. Although intensive multi-agent chemotherapy can achieve high complete remission rates, it is associated with substantial toxicity, morbidity, and sometimes treatment-related mortality. This retrospective, single-center observational study aims to characterize the short- and long-term complications of intensive first-line treatment in adults with Burkitt lymphoma managed at Strasbourg University Hospitals.

The study will evaluate treatment-related toxicities, overall survival at five years, and progression-free survival at 24 months. Secondary objectives include assessing treatment delays, chemotherapy dose reductions, and their associations with toxicity, disease location at diagnosis, and survival.

All eligible adult patients diagnosed with Burkitt lymphoma or managed for this condition at Strasbourg University Hospitals and the ICANS between January 1, 2009, and December 31, 2025, will be considered. The study will use retrospective medical record data, with no a priori sample size calculation because of the rarity of the disease and the single-center design.
title: Toxicity of Intensive First-Line Treatment for Adult Burkitt Lymphoma: A Retrospective Observational Study

brief_summary: For patients with metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) who have failed two or more lines of standard therapy, treatment options are extremely limited, and the prognosis remains poor, with objective response rates (ORRs) generally below 5%. This is particularly challenging for patients with microsatellite-stable (MSS)/proficient mismatch repair (pMMR) tumors, who constitute the vast majority of patients with mCRC. The immunologically "cold" tumor microenvironment (TME) in these patients contributes to widespread primary resistance to PD-1 inhibitor monotherapy. A key mechanism underlying this resistance is the sustained activation of JAK/STAT signaling, which promotes immunosuppression mediated by myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs) and other immunosuppressive components, thereby limiting T-cell activity and the efficacy of strategies that solely reinvigorate T cells. To address this challenge, we propose an innovative combination strategy aimed at remodeling the TME and alleviating immunosuppression. We hypothesize that ivarmacitinib, a highly selective JAK1 inhibitor, may attenuate the immunosuppressive TME through modulation of JAK/STAT signaling, potentially converting "cold" tumors into "hot" tumors and enhancing the antitumor activity of camrelizumab, a PD-1 inhibitor, in combination with fruquintinib, a tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI). Accordingly, we designed a single-arm, single-center, exploratory phase II clinical study enrolling 33 patients with mCRC who have failed multiple lines of prior therapy. The study aims to evaluate the ORR, survival outcomes, and safety of this combination regimen. The findings are expected to provide preliminary evidence for a potential new therapeutic approach for this heavily pretreated patient population and establish a foundation for subsequent larger confirmatory studies.
title: Ivarmacitinib Combined With Camrelizumab and Fruquintinib for Patients With Metastatic Colorectal Cancer After Failure of Second-line or Later Treatment, A Phase II Study

brief_summary:
Small cell lung cancer (SCLC) is a type of lung cancer that accounts for approximately 15-17% of all lung cancers. It is characterized by aggressive and rapid growth and early spread to distant sites. Extensive stage-small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC) includes cases where disease has spread beyond one side of the chest. This study will evaluate the safety and efficacy of ABBV-706 in combination with atezolizumab and alveltamig in previously untreated ES-SCLC.

ABBV-706 and alveltamig are investigational drugs being developed for the treatment of ES-SCLC. This is an open-label study, meaning participants and doctors know which treatment is being given. Participants are placed into 1 of 2 treatment arms. Each arm receives a different dose of ABBV-706 in combination with alveltamig and atezolizumab. Adult participants with a diagnosis of previously untreated extensive stage-small cell lung cancer will be enrolled. Around 80 participants will be enrolled in the study at approximately 25 sites worldwide.

Participants will receive intravenous (IV) infusion of ABBV-706 in combination with IV infusion of atezolizumab and IV infusion of alveltamig. The estimated duration of the study is approximately 61 months.

There may be higher treatment burden for participants in this trial compared to their standard of care due to study procedures. Participants will attend regular visits during the study at a hospital or clinic. The effects of the treatment will be checked by medical assessments, blood tests, imaging scans, checking for side effects and completing questionnaires.
primary_outcomes: Objective Response (OR) as Measured by Overall Response Rate (ORR) Based on Blinded Independent Central Review (BICR) Assessment Per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors version 1.1 (RECIST v1.1)
Number of Participants with Adverse Events (AEs)
title: A Study to Assess Adverse Events and Change in Disease Activity of Intravenous (IV) ABBV-706 in Combination With Alveltamig and Atezolizumab for Adults Participants With Extensive Stage-Small Cell Lung Cancer

brief_summary:
The purpose of this study is to study how avatrombopag (the study drug) may prevent certain side effects in adults with lymphoma and myeloma getting cancer treatment (CAR-T cell therapy). CAR (Chimeric Antigen Receptor) -T cell therapy is a common way to treat lymphoma and myeloma. However, during this kind of cell therapy a patient is at risk of developing lower-than-normal blood cell counts, including:

* Red Blood Cells - important for many functions such as moving oxygen from the lungs to the body and moving carbon dioxide (CO2) back to the lungs
* White Blood Cells - help fight against infection(s)
* Platelets - help stop bleeding by forming clots when there is an injury

When a person's platelet counts are lower than normal, this is called "thrombocytopenia". If you have thrombocytopenia, your body has a harder time stopping a bleed when there is an injury to a blood vessel. Thrombocytopenia over time may require additional treatments such as blood transfusions (getting extra platelets).

Avatrombopag is a drug that has been shown to increase platelet numbers in people with other kinds of conditions. This study is trying to find out if taking avatrombopag both before and after CAR-T cell therapy will prevent platelet counts from getting too low.

This is a research study to see if taking avatrombopag (in the form of pills) before, during, and after CAR-T cell therapy will reduce the chance of having thrombocytopenia as a side effect.

This study is for people who are at high risk of thrombocytopenia after CAR T-Cell Therapy.
title: Time-limited Treatment With Avatrombopag Pre- and Post-CAR T-cell Therapy to Prevent Post-CAR T-cell Cytopenias

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether high-intensity laser therapy applied before exercise reduces the loss of handgrip strength, muscle stiffness, and pain after a tiring forearm exercise in healthy adults. This therapy delivers laser light through the skin to the underlying tissues.

The main questions this study aims to answer are:

Does laser therapy reduce the loss of handgrip strength after exercise compared with placebo treatment?

Does laser therapy reduce the increase in forearm muscle stiffness after exercise?

Does laser therapy reduce pain after exercise?

Researchers will compare active laser therapy with placebo laser treatment to assess whether the active treatment affects the muscles' response to exercise. Each participant will receive both treatments on separate visits. The order of treatments will be assigned by chance.

Participants will attend two laboratory visits at the Faculty of Health Sciences, University of Primorska, Slovenia. At one visit, they will receive active laser therapy over the muscles that bend the wrist in their dominant forearm. At the other visit, they will receive placebo treatment over the same area.

At each visit, participants will:

Rest before the initial measurements.

Have their handgrip strength, forearm muscle stiffness, and pain measured before treatment.

Receive active laser therapy or placebo treatment.

Wait five minutes before starting the exercise procedure.

Complete a wrist-strength test, then hold a muscle contraction at half of their maximum wrist-bending strength until they can no longer maintain the required force.

Have their handgrip strength, muscle stiffness, and pain measured again immediately after exercise and five and fifteen minutes later.

Handgrip strength will be measured by squeezing a handheld device. Muscle stiffness will be measured using a device that applies a brief, gentle mechanical tap to the skin over the muscle. Participants will rate their pain using a visual scale.

Participants will be asked to avoid strenuous physical activity for at least 24 hours before each visit and to keep their diet and regular supplement use similar before both visits.

The main outcome is the change in handgrip strength from before treatment to after exercise. Changes in muscle stiffness and pain will also be compared between the two treatments. Researchers expect active laser therapy to result in a smaller decrease in handgrip strength and smaller increases in muscle stiffness and pain than placebo treatment.
interventions: High-Intensity Laser Therapy (HILT) and sham HILT
title: Acute Effects of High-Intensity Laser Therapy on Pain, Muscle Stiffness, and Grip Strength in Healthy Adults
